operations.description:
Log in an existing seller account with email and password.

This operation authenticates a merchant who already has a seller account and wants to start a signed-in session. It is the normal sign-in step after registration and any approval workflow.

The request body contains the seller login DTO. If credentials are valid and the account is allowed to sign in, the server returns the authorized seller token payload. Authentication failures must not reveal whether the email address exists or the password was wrong.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials for authenticating an existing merchant account.

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller credentials and tokens issued after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the seller refresh token, ensure it is unexpired and tied to a valid seller session, and issue a new authorized token set. Reject malformed, expired, revoked, or otherwise invalid refresh tokens. Do not require the password again when the refresh token is valid.
operations.description:
Renew a seller's authentication tokens using a refresh token.

This operation keeps a seller session active without requiring the merchant to sign in again with email and password. It is part of the standard token renewal flow for the seller actor.

The request body uses the seller refresh DTO. When the refresh token is valid and tied to an active seller session, the server returns a new authorized token payload. Invalid or expired tokens must be rejected.

requestBody.description: Seller refresh token payload used to obtain new authentication tokens.

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller credentials and tokens issued after successful refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Validate administrator registration input, create the administrator account record, and issue authorized tokens when registration succeeds. Enforce uniqueness and password validation, and return a client error for invalid or conflicting credentials.
operations.description:
Register a new administrator account and return authentication tokens.

This endpoint creates a new administrator identity for the mall platform and returns the authorized token payload on success. It is the registration entry point for administrator accounts when the system allows creating them.

If the request fails validation or conflicts with an existing administrator account, the endpoint must return an appropriate client error. On success, the response contains the administrator's authorization payload for subsequent authenticated requests.

requestBody.description: Administrator registration credentials.

responseBody.description: Administrator authentication result containing issued tokens.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate administrator login credentials against the administrator account store, verify that the account is allowed to sign in, and issue authorized tokens. Reject invalid credentials and account states that block access, such as bans or other sign-in restrictions.
operations.description:
Authenticate an administrator with email and password and return tokens.

This endpoint verifies the administrator's credentials and produces the authorized token payload on success. It is the standard sign-in flow for administrator users.

If the credentials are invalid or the account is blocked from access, the endpoint must fail with an authentication or authorization error. A successful response returns the token pair needed for subsequent authenticated requests.

requestBody.description: Administrator login credentials.

responseBody.description: Administrator authentication result containing issued tokens.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the administrator refresh token, confirm it is still usable for the administrator session, and issue a new authorized token payload. Reject expired, revoked, malformed, or otherwise invalid refresh tokens.
operations.description:
Refresh an administrator session and return new authentication tokens.

This endpoint renews administrator access when the client presents a valid refresh token. It is used to continue an existing session without requiring the administrator to sign in again.

If the refresh token is expired, invalid, or no longer associated with a valid administrator session, the endpoint must fail with an authentication error. On success, the response contains a fresh authorized token payload.

requestBody.description: Administrator refresh token payload.

responseBody.description: Administrator authentication result containing issued tokens.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Search and browse customer accounts with pagination and filters.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of registered customer accounts for administrative browsing and account management workflows. It is intended for searching by account identity or status and for navigating through the customer registry in a controlled page-based format.

Customer accounts are the authenticated shopper identities for the platform. The list reflects persisted customer records and must respect account availability rules, including account state checks defined by the business rules. Results should be stable across pages, and empty result sets must be returned successfully when no records match the criteria.

If the requested page exceeds the available result set, the response should still be a valid empty page. Validation errors should be returned for malformed search criteria, invalid pagination values, or unsupported sort options.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_customers table as the source of truth for customer accounts.
Apply request filters and pagination in the service layer, then return a paginated summary list.

Support search and sorting on customer-account fields that are appropriate for browsing, and ensure the query remains consistent with the customer account lifecycle rules. The endpoint must not expose password credentials or other sensitive auth data. If account status is part of the search criteria, treat unavailable states according to business rules. Use a deterministic sort order when the client does not provide one, and make pagination stable across repeated requests.

Reject invalid pagination values, malformed search terms, and unsupported sort directions with a validation error. If no customers match, return an empty page rather than an error. This endpoint is read-only and must not modify any customer data.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary of customer accounts matching the search criteria.

requestBody.description: Customer search criteria including pagination, filtering, and sorting options for browsing the customer registry.

operations.description:
Returns one customer account by its unique identifier.

This operation retrieves the customer account record used for sign-in and account status control. It is intended for account detail inspection and management flows where the caller needs the current customer identity and lifecycle state.

The underlying customer table stores authentication data and status, while the customer profile is maintained separately. For security, credential material such as the password hash must not be exposed in the API response, even though it exists in storage.

If the customer does not exist, the service should return a not found error. If the account is removed or otherwise inaccessible under the caller's permissions, the response should fail cleanly without exposing unrelated account data.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the customer by UUID primary key from mall_platform_customers.
Verify that the row exists and is accessible under the current authorization rules.
Never serialize password_hash in the response payload, even though the database contains it.
If the implementation needs customer ownership checks, enforce them here; otherwise allow administrator-level access through the auth layer.
Return a single customer entity response and keep customer profile fields out of this endpoint because they belong to mall_platform_customer_profiles.
If no matching record is found, return a not found error.

responseBody.description: The customer account record for the requested identifier, excluding sensitive credential material.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the customer account to retrieve (UUID).
parameters.name: customerId

operations.description:
Update the signed-in customer’s profile information.

This operation lets an authenticated customer change the display name and phone number stored in their customer profile. The profile represents the customer’s personal identity details on the platform, and the update applies only to those profile fields.

The server must resolve the profile from the current authenticated customer account rather than accepting an identifier in the path. Validation must reject incomplete or unsuitable profile data, and the profile must remain unchanged when validation fails. This operation does not modify account credentials, shipping addresses, or order records.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the customer profile from the authenticated session context and load the single profile owned by that customer account.
Validate the request body before persisting any change. Only display name and phone number are allowed to change. Reject the request if either value is missing, malformed, or otherwise unsuitable for normal customer use.
Apply the update only to the customer profile row and do not touch the customer account, addresses, orders, or authentication data. If the profile is unavailable because the account was deleted or the profile no longer exists, return a not-found or unavailable error and do not recreate the record.
Persist the new values atomically and return the updated profile after success.

responseBody.description: The updated customer profile for the signed-in customer, including the current display name and phone number.

requestBody.description: The new customer profile values to apply to the signed-in customer’s profile.

operations.description:
Search and browse platform session records with pagination and filters.

This operation returns a paginated list of session summaries for administrative inspection and account oversight. It is intended for browsing authenticated session records rather than creating or managing sessions directly, and it should support search, filtering, and sorting where those criteria are available in the underlying session data.

Session records belong to customer, seller, or administrator authentication flows. The service must enforce authorization before returning any data and must never expose sensitive session secrets or tokens in the summary payload. Invalid filters, unsupported session scopes, or malformed pagination values should be rejected with a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the session store through the administrative session browsing service with pagination, optional filters, and sorting.
Use the relevant session table or a unified read model backed by the available customer, seller, and administrator session records, depending on the platform implementation.
Return only non-sensitive summary fields needed for browsing, such as identifiers, account references, status, and timestamps if those fields exist in the schema.
Validate all search inputs, clamp or reject invalid paging values, and return an empty page when no records match.
Do not include authentication secrets, refresh tokens, or any material intended only for login/session verification flows.

responseBody.description: Paginated session summaries for browsing and administrative review.

requestBody.description: Session search criteria including pagination, optional filters, and sort options.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current session record by its identifier.

This endpoint returns the stored session metadata for an authenticated customer, seller, or administrator session, including creation time, expiration time, and request context captured when the session was created. It is intended for session inspection and verification during authenticated use of the platform.

Access to this resource must respect the signed-in account context. The implementation must ensure that a user can only retrieve a session they are allowed to view, and that expired or invalid sessions are rejected consistently. If the session does not exist, belongs to another account, or is no longer valid, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Load the session record by UUID primary key from the appropriate session store. Validate that the session exists and is still valid according to its expired_at timestamp before returning it. Enforce account scoping so the requester cannot inspect another account's session unless the platform explicitly grants that access in higher-layer authorization rules. Do not return any secret token value; only expose safe metadata such as id, account reference, ip, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at. If the record is missing, expired, or unauthorized, return the corresponding error without leaking whether another account owns the session.

responseBody.description: The session record for the requested authenticated session, including safe session metadata and expiration information.

parameters.description: The UUID of the session to retrieve.
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Search password reset records across customer, seller, and administrator accounts.

This endpoint provides a paginated operational view of password reset activity for the marketplace platform. It is intended for support, moderation, and audit-related review of recovery requests, and it returns only safe metadata such as the owning account reference, expiration state, consumption state, and lifecycle timestamps.

The service must not expose raw reset tokens or password hashes. Implementations should normalize results from the three password reset tables into a single pageable collection so clients can filter and browse recovery records without knowing which account type owns each row.

Because these records are sensitive and time-bound, validation should reject unsupported filters, invalid date ranges, and incompatible combinations before any database query is executed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only unified search over mall_platform_customer_password_resets, mall_platform_seller_password_resets, and mall_platform_administrator_password_resets.

Support pagination, sorting, and filters for account type, owning account identifier, lifecycle state, and created/expired time windows. Default ordering should be newest first by created_at. Do not include raw token, reset_token, or password_hash fields in any response. If the query needs to identify the owning account, join only to resolve safe display fields such as email or account status, and still exclude secret values.

For customer resets, read mall_platform_customer_password_resets using mall_platform_customer_id, expired_at, used_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. For seller resets, read mall_platform_seller_password_resets using seller_account_id, expired_at, consumed_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. For administrator resets, read mall_platform_administrator_password_resets using administrator_id, expired_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The endpoint must never mutate any reset row, consume tokens, or mark usage as a side effect of searching.

responseBody.description: Paginated password reset summaries across customer, seller, and administrator accounts, excluding secret token values.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for password reset records, including account type, owner reference, lifecycle state, date ranges, pagination, and sorting.

operations.description:
Retrieve a customer password reset record by its identifier.

This endpoint returns the password reset row associated with the given UUID, including the owning customer reference, token, expiration time, optional used time, and audit timestamps. It is intended for account recovery inspection and validation of the reset lifecycle.

The record is read-only through this endpoint. The server should validate the UUID path parameter before querying, return not found when the record does not exist, and avoid exposing any fields that are not present in the database schema.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Look up one row in mall_platform_customer_password_resets by primary key using passwordResetId as a UUID. Validate the path parameter format before querying. Return the stored fields id, mall_platform_customer_id, token, expired_at, used_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at exactly as persisted. Do not join other tables or infer extra properties. If no row matches, return a not-found error. Preserve the existing row data as-is for read access.

responseBody.description: A single customer password reset record with its recovery metadata.

parameters.description: The password reset record identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: passwordResetId

operations.description:
Search and paginate seller accounts.

This endpoint provides a filtered seller list for moderation and administrative browsing. It is designed to surface seller identity, approval state, rejection information, and lifecycle visibility without exposing authentication secrets.

Use this operation when a client needs to browse sellers by status, creation time, or other supported list criteria. The implementation must respect account visibility rules, return stable paginated results, and reject invalid pagination, search, or sort inputs. Password hashes must never be included in the response.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_sellers table for browseable seller accounts.
Apply search and filters against email, status, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at visibility according to the request schema and authorization context. Support sorting and pagination for large result sets, defaulting to newest-first when no sort is provided.
Return summary rows only and never expose password_hash. Include moderation fields such as status and rejection_reason so administrators can distinguish pending, approved, rejected, suspended, and banned sellers. Validate unsupported filter values, malformed pagination, and unknown sort keys with standard input errors.

responseBody.description: Paginated seller summaries for administrative browsing.

requestBody.description: Seller search criteria including pagination, keyword search, status filters, and sort options.

operations.description:
Retrieve one seller account together with its public shop profile.

This endpoint returns the merchant account used across the marketplace and the public profile information shown to customers on seller pages and product pages. It is useful for profile display, order-history context, and administrative review because it exposes the current seller status and public shop identity in one read.

The seller account represents the merchant identity, while the related shop profile contains the editable branding data such as shop name, description, and logo. If the seller is pending, approved, or rejected, clients can use the returned status to render that state, and they can display the rejection reason when the approval workflow has one. If the seller does not exist, the service must return a not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Load the seller account by sellerId and join the associated public seller profile for presentation. Return the seller entity with its current approval/status information and any public profile fields needed by the UI. Do not include password hashes, sessions, reset tokens, or other authentication artifacts. If the seller is missing, return 404. If the current actor is not permitted to view the seller, return 403. This operation must be read-only and must not modify seller approval, profile, suspension, or snapshot data. If historical shop identity is needed for order history, it should be sourced from preserved snapshots rather than the live profile record.

responseBody.description: The seller account and public shop profile details for one seller.

parameters.description: The seller account identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: sellerId

operations.description:
Lists administrator approval requests for governance review.

This endpoint returns a paginated queue of administrator approval requests, including request status and review metadata needed by super administrators to evaluate pending applications. It is intended for review workflows rather than public browsing, and the result set should support filtering by status, searching by applicant or reason text, and sorting by submission or review timestamps.

Only authorized super administrators should access this endpoint. Pending requests remain visible until they are approved or rejected, and rejected or approved records should still be retrievable through the same list for audit and follow-up purposes. If the caller is not authorized, return an access error. If the request body contains invalid pagination or filter values, return a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests with pagination, status filtering, free-text search, and sortable ordering.
Use the request body as a search specification rather than path parameters because the list may need multiple filters.
Filter by approval request status and search across applicant-related text fields and submitted reason fields available in the schema.
Return the list as paginated summary rows ordered by the requested sort field, with a stable secondary sort for deterministic paging.
If the user lacks super administrator privileges, reject the request before querying.
If pagination values are out of range or sort keys are unsupported, return a validation error.
Do not include mutable workflow actions in this endpoint; approval and rejection must be handled by dedicated update operations.

responseBody.description: Paginated administrator approval request summaries for review queues and governance oversight.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for administrator approval request review.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single administrator account by identifier.

This endpoint returns the persisted administrator record used for platform governance, moderation, and oversight. It is intended for authorized administrative users who need to inspect one administrator account’s current state and account-level metadata.

The response is read-only and does not include sessions, passwords, or other authentication data. If the administrator does not exist, the service should return a not-found error. Access must remain restricted according to administrator governance permissions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Load the administrator record from mall_platform_administrators using the administratorId path parameter. Validate that the parameter is a UUID before querying. Return a not-found error when no row matches, and do not join session or password reset tables. The response must map directly to the administrator entity schema and must not expose secrets or derived auth state.

responseBody.description: The full administrator account record for the requested identifier.

parameters.description: The administrator account identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: administratorId

operations.description:
Searches administrator approval requests for super administrator review.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of administrator approval requests so super administrators can review pending applications and inspect each request's current status and recorded outcome. Each summary reflects the applicant's reason for applying, the review state, and the decision trail used for platform governance.

The list is intended for oversight rather than general account browsing. It should support paging, filtering, and sorting according to the platform's browsing rules, and it must keep approved, rejected, and pending requests visible according to the stored status data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests table with pagination, keyword search, status filtering, and stable sorting. Support status filters for pending, approved, and rejected, and only expose fields appropriate to an administrative summary list. Do not mutate any request rows in this operation.

Apply pagination whenever the result set exceeds a single page. Default sorting should be newest-first unless the request specifies another valid order. Reject invalid filter values before querying. If the caller lacks administrator review privileges, return an authorization error. Keep the operation read-only and use the existing approval-request status values exactly as stored in the domain model.

responseBody.description: Paginated administrator approval request summaries for review and governance oversight.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for administrator approval request review.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single administrator approval request for governance review.

This endpoint returns the current approval request record so an authorized administrator can inspect the applicant reference, the reason submitted with the request, the current review status, and any stored decision details. It is a read-only detail view and does not change the request lifecycle.

Access to this endpoint should be restricted to privileged administrative actors that are allowed to review administrator access requests. If the approval request does not exist, the server should return a not found response. If the caller lacks permission, the server should return a forbidden response.

Historical snapshot records are preserved separately for audit and dispute resolution. This endpoint exposes only the current active request state.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the administrator approval request row from mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests by UUID primary key.
Return the persisted applicant reference, submitted reason, current review status, reviewer decision outcome, and any lifecycle timestamps stored in the base table.
Do not aggregate snapshot history into this response; snapshots are handled by their own read endpoints.
Enforce governance authorization so only privileged administrative users can access the record.
Return 404 when the identifier does not match an existing request, and 403 when the caller is not allowed to review administrator requests.

responseBody.description: The current administrator approval request record with its persisted review state and decision metadata.

parameters.description: The administrator approval request identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: approvalRequestId

operations.description:
Returns the signed-in customer's current profile information.

This operation is limited to the authenticated customer account and exposes the customer-facing identity details stored in the customer profile, specifically the display name and phone number. It does not include credentials, addresses, or order history.

The customer must be signed in to access this resource. If authentication is missing or invalid, the request must be rejected. If the profile cannot be resolved for the current customer account, the service should return the appropriate not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the current customer from the authentication context and load the related row from mall_platform_customer_profiles. Do not accept any client-supplied customer identifier because the endpoint is scoped to the current session.

Return the profile fields that exist in the schema and are intended for customer-facing identity: display name and phone number. If authentication fails, return 401. If the authenticated customer has no profile row, return 404. Do not query or mutate any other tables for this operation unless middleware requires session validation.

responseBody.description: The authenticated customer's profile record containing the current display name and phone number.

operations.description:
Returns a paginated list of the authenticated customer's saved shipping addresses.

This operation is used to browse address records that belong to the current customer account, including the default shipping address used during checkout. Results should reflect the customer's own saved addresses only, and the response is suitable for address management screens and checkout address selection.

If filtering or pagination cannot be applied, the request should fail with a validation or authorization error rather than returning another customer's data. The address list must remain consistent if the request fails.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_shipping_addresses table for the authenticated customer only.
Apply pagination, keyword search, and sorting from the request body. Search should match recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, and country when supported by the request schema.
Ensure the result set is restricted to addresses owned by the current customer account. Include default-address information if present in the schema.
Return a paginated summary view ordered according to the requested sort. If the customer has no addresses, return an empty page rather than an error.
Reject requests that attempt to access or infer other customers' addresses. Do not mutate any data in this operation.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary list of the authenticated customer's shipping addresses.

requestBody.description: Pagination, search, and sorting criteria for browsing the customer's saved shipping addresses.

operations.description:
Create a new shipping address for the authenticated customer.

This endpoint stores a reusable delivery destination for checkout and order fulfillment. The new address belongs to the signed-in customer account and becomes available for future orders immediately after creation.

The address must include recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, and country. The customer may also mark the address as the default shipping address. If validation fails, the address is not created and the saved address list remains unchanged.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new row into mall_platform_shipping_addresses for the authenticated customer. Derive customer_id from the current session and reject any client-supplied ownership field. Validate recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country, and is_default from the request body. Do not accept id, customer_id, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at from the client.

If is_default is true, perform the default-address swap inside a single transaction so the previous default for the same customer is cleared before the new row is inserted, preserving the @@unique([customer_id, is_default]) constraint. Populate created_at and updated_at automatically. On any failure, roll back the transaction so no partial address state is persisted.

responseBody.description: The created shipping address record for the authenticated customer.

requestBody.description: Fields required to create a saved shipping address for the authenticated customer.

operations.description:
Retrieve one saved shipping address belonging to the current customer.

This operation returns the full delivery destination record so the customer can review recipient details, contact information, and location fields before using the address for checkout or editing it later. The address must belong to the authenticated customer account; otherwise, the request is rejected.

The returned address represents a customer-managed delivery destination. It is one entry in the customer address book and may be used as a checkout destination or as the default shipping address if the customer has marked it that way. If the address does not exist, has been removed, or is not owned by the caller, the service returns a not-found or forbidden-style error consistent with the platform authorization rules.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the shipping address row by its primary identifier and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer before returning it. Use a single record lookup with ownership enforcement so a customer cannot read another customer’s address. Return the full entity fields that exist in the shipping address schema, including recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, country, and any default-selection metadata that is present in the actual table definition.

If the record is missing, return a not-found error. If the record exists but belongs to another customer, return a forbidden or not-found style response according to the platform’s access-control convention. Do not expose any unrelated internal fields or session data. No mutation occurs in this operation.

responseBody.description: The full saved shipping address record for the authenticated customer.

parameters.description: The shipping address identifier (UUID) for the customer-owned saved address.
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

operations.description:
Updates a saved shipping address owned by the current customer.

The customer can change the recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, country, and default-address flag for an existing saved destination. The address stays linked to the same customer account and remains available for checkout after the update.

The service must verify that the record exists and belongs to the authenticated customer before applying any change. If validation fails, the address is missing, or the record belongs to another customer, the request must fail without changing any saved address data.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shipping address by UUID, confirm ownership for the authenticated customer, and apply the update in a single transaction. Only allow updates to recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country, and is_default.

Reject any attempt to modify id, customer_id, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at through this endpoint. If is_default is set to true, ensure the customer's default-address uniqueness rule remains valid by clearing the default flag from any other active address for the same customer within the same transaction before saving the updated record. On any failure, roll back the transaction so no partial update is persisted.

responseBody.description: The shipping address after the update has been successfully saved.

parameters.description: The shipping address identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

requestBody.description: Editable delivery details for the selected shipping address.

operations.description:
Delete a saved shipping address owned by the current customer.

This operation removes one address from the customer's saved address list so it can no longer be used during checkout. If the address is currently marked as the default shipping address, the system clears that default designation before removing the record to keep the customer's address state valid.

The request is safe when the address is already missing or has been deleted before: the system must leave the remaining saved addresses unchanged and must not partially update any address record on failure. Other saved addresses remain available after a successful deletion.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Look up the shipping address by shippingAddressId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer. If the address does not exist, handle the request safely as a no-op so the customer's saved address list remains unchanged.

If the address exists and is the customer's default address, clear the default flag before deleting the row. Perform the default-clear and delete in a single transaction so a failure cannot leave the customer with a broken default reference or a partially updated address list. Do not modify any other saved addresses.

Return no content on success. Enforce ownership checks and return not found or forbidden when the target address is inaccessible to the caller.

parameters.description: The identifier of the shipping address to remove from the customer's saved address list.
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

operations.description:
Set a saved shipping address as the customer's default delivery address.

This operation marks one existing shipping address as the preferred checkout destination for the owning customer. If another saved address was previously marked as default, the service must replace that designation so only one default address remains for the customer.

Ownership is enforced strictly: the caller may only change a shipping address that belongs to their own customer account. If the address does not exist or belongs to another customer, the request must be rejected and no address records may be modified.

The selected address must still satisfy shipping-address validation rules. If the operation fails for any reason, the customer's saved address list must remain unchanged and no partial update may be applied.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shipping address by shippingAddressId and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject with 404 when the address does not exist and with 403 when it exists but is owned by another customer.

Within a transaction, clear the default designation from any other shipping address rows belonging to the same customer, then mark the target address as default. Ensure the operation leaves exactly one default address for that customer after success.

Do not update address content fields. Do not create or remove address rows. If the target address is already the default address, the operation may succeed idempotently without changing persisted state.

If validation or persistence fails, roll back the transaction so the customer's address list remains unchanged. Return the updated shipping address entity or the canonical address representation used by the service layer.

responseBody.description: The shipping address after its default status has been applied.

parameters.description: The shipping address identifier in the customer's account.
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

operations.description:
Returns the authenticated customer account for the current session.

This endpoint is available only to registered and logged-in customers. It provides the account-level identity and status needed by account settings screens and other customer-owned workflows. Guest access is not allowed, and requests from deleted or banned accounts must be rejected.

The returned account data should reflect the current persisted customer account record. If the implementation includes related profile data in the same response, it must be composed from the customer account and its linked customer profile without exposing other users' data. Authentication and authorization failures should return the appropriate access error response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated customer from the current session and load the corresponding mall_platform_customers record. Enforce that the caller is a registered customer and that the account is active; reject unauthenticated requests, deleted-account access, and banned-account access. Return the single customer account entity for the current user only.

Do not accept any path or query identifier for account selection because this endpoint is always scoped to the logged-in principal. If the customer profile is composed into the response by the application layer, join the linked mall_platform_customer_profiles row by customer account relationship and omit any unrelated records. Preserve the existing account state exactly as stored.

responseBody.description: The authenticated customer's current account record.

operations.description:
Returns a paginated list of profile snapshot records for browsing historical profile changes.

This endpoint is intended for viewing immutable history entries created when a profile is updated. It supports search, filtering, pagination, and sorting so authorized users can review change history for dispute resolution and audit purposes. Snapshot records are read-only and must never be modified through this API.

The response should reflect the profile snapshot model preserved by the platform, including change timestamps and before/after values when available. Access control must ensure that only the profile owner and administrators can view the relevant snapshot history for the profile scope represented by this endpoint.

If no snapshots match the filters, the endpoint returns an empty page rather than an error. Invalid pagination, sorting, or filter values should be rejected with a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the immutable profile snapshot history using pagination and optional filters. Build the query against the profile snapshot table for the current profile scope represented by the route. Support server-side pagination, free-text search if snapshot metadata supports it, and stable sorting by change timestamp descending by default.

Do not expose any mutation behavior because snapshots are immutable historical records. Do not attempt to update, delete, or recreate snapshot rows from this endpoint. If access control is enforced at the service layer, require the caller to be the profile owner or an administrator with dispute-review privileges, and filter out records outside the caller's authorization scope.

Return only summary fields needed for list browsing, not the entire nested history payload, unless the summary component definition explicitly includes them. When no records are found, return an empty paginated result. Validate pagination bounds and sort fields before querying, and return a standard not-found or forbidden error when the profile scope cannot be resolved or accessed.

responseBody.description: Paginated profile snapshot history records for browsing immutable change history.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for browsing profile snapshot history.

operations.description:
Retrieve a customer profile snapshot for historical review and dispute resolution.

This endpoint returns one immutable snapshot created after a successful customer profile edit. The snapshot preserves the previous state of the profile so consumers can inspect what changed without affecting the current customer profile.

Use this operation when showing profile change history to the profile owner or to an authorized administrator. If the snapshot does not exist, the service should return a not-found error. Because snapshots are immutable records, this resource does not support update or delete behavior.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Load the customer profile snapshot by its unique identifier and return the full stored snapshot entity. Treat the record as immutable history; do not recompute it from the live profile table. Return 404 if no snapshot exists for the provided ID. Enforce authorization so only the profile owner and authorized administrators can access the snapshot. If the schema includes normalized detail tables for snapshot deltas, include them in the response composition; otherwise return the snapshot entity itself.

responseBody.description: The immutable customer profile snapshot, including the preserved before-and-after values needed for history inspection.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the customer profile snapshot to retrieve.
parameters.name: snapshotId

operations.description:
Returns a paginated list of marketplace categories with search, filtering, and sorting support.

This endpoint is used to browse administrator-managed categories and their direct subcategories under the one-level nesting rule. It supports customer-facing discovery flows and internal management screens that need a filtered category list.

Each result should represent a category record with enough context for clients to render the category name, description, and direct parent-child relationship correctly. If no records match the search criteria, the response should be an empty page rather than an error.

Requests that attempt to express unsupported deeper hierarchy levels, or otherwise violate the one-level category structure, should be rejected before query execution.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_categories with pagination, keyword search, and sort options. Support filtering by category name and parent category scope so clients can browse top-level categories and direct subcategories while respecting the one-level nesting rule.

Apply stable ordering for pagination and return summary fields only. If the client needs browsing context, include parent category information in the summary projection. Reject invalid page values, unsupported filters, and sort keys that are not part of the category list contract. Return an empty page when no records match.

responseBody.description: Paginated category summaries for browsing and management list screens.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for browsing categories, including name filters, parent-category scope, and sort options.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single category and its direct subcategory structure.

This operation returns the full category record so customers can understand how products are organized and administrators can inspect category definitions. Categories are administrator-managed, and the returned structure must respect the one-level nesting rule by exposing only direct subcategories.

If the category does not exist, the server should return a not found error. Customer-facing visibility rules must be respected so removed categories do not appear in browsing contexts, while valid category details remain available to authorized callers.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load one row from mall_platform_categories by its primary UUID identifier. Validate that categoryId is a UUID and return the complete category entity, including any directly related subcategory data required by the domain model. Do not traverse beyond one level of nesting because deeper category chains are not allowed.

Apply read authorization according to the actor rules: customers may read categories for browsing, and administrators may inspect category records directly. If the category is missing, return 404. If the category is unavailable in browsing because it has been deleted, the service should exclude it from customer-facing flows. This endpoint is read-only and must not change any data.

responseBody.description: Full category details including its identity, name, description, and direct subcategory information.

parameters.description: The category identifier in global scope.
parameters.name: categoryId

operations.description:
Search products within a category.

This endpoint returns a paginated set of products that belong to the specified category and is intended for customer-facing category browsing screens. It supports filtering and sorting so customers can discover products within the administrator-managed catalog structure.

Category browsing must exclude deleted categories from results and must not expose products through deleted category listings. The response is optimized for listing cards and returns summary data only, not full product detail records. If the category does not exist or is not available for browsing, the request should fail using the platform’s standard not-found handling.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Confirm the requested category exists and is available for browsing before querying products. If the category is deleted or otherwise unavailable, return a not-found error consistent with category browsing behavior.

Query mall_platform_products for products belonging to the category. Apply platform visibility rules so only products eligible for customer browsing are included. If summary projections require seller shop name, thumbnail image, or review aggregates, join the relevant product, product image, seller profile, and review data in a read-only query.

Apply request filters for keyword search, price range, in-stock-only constraints, and sorting. Use a stable order for pagination and return an empty page when no products match. Do not mutate category or product data in this operation.

responseBody.description: Paginated product summaries for the selected category browsing view.

parameters.description: The category identifier in scope for this product listing (global unique identifier).
parameters.name: categoryId

requestBody.description: Category product search criteria including pagination, keyword search, filtering, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Create a new marketplace category or direct subcategory.

This operation lets an administrator add a category record used to organize products across the platform. Categories are centrally managed and visible to customers for browsing, while the system enforces the one-level nesting rule so a subcategory can belong only to a top-level category.

Only administrators may call this endpoint. If the request attempts to create an invalid hierarchy, such as a deeper nested subcategory or a structurally inconsistent parent-child relationship, the request must be rejected and no category data should be persisted. The created category becomes immediately available for product assignment and category browsing once validation succeeds.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Insert a new row into mall_platform_categories after validating administrator privileges and category structure rules. Validate the category name and description against the category rules, and if a parent reference is provided, ensure it points to an existing top-level category so only one level of nesting is possible. Reject any attempt to create deeper nesting or an inconsistent parent-child structure before writing to the database. If the schema supports a parent category foreign key, persist it; otherwise, create a top-level category only. Return the created category entity after commit. Use a transaction if additional integrity checks are required. Surface authorization failures as forbidden, missing parent or category references as not found, and structural violations as validation errors.

responseBody.description: The newly created category record, including its persisted identity and hierarchy information.

requestBody.description: Category details to create, including the category name, description, and optional parent category reference when creating a direct subcategory.

operations.description:
Update an existing marketplace category.

Administrators use this operation to change a category's name or description while preserving the platform's one-level category hierarchy. Categories are part of the browsing structure for products, so any update must keep the hierarchy valid and must not introduce deeper nesting.

This operation is restricted to administrators. If the category does not exist, the server should return not found. If the requested change would violate the category structure rules, the server should reject the request with a validation error before saving any changes.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Authenticate the caller as an administrator before processing the request. Load the category by category_id and return 404 if it does not exist.

Validate the update payload against the category rules. The category may be updated for its editable fields, and any hierarchy-related values must preserve the one-level nesting rule. A subcategory must never be converted into a deeper descendant structure, and any invalid parent-child assignment must be rejected before persistence.

Apply the change in a transaction and return the updated category record. No product rows are directly modified by this endpoint, but category changes must remain consistent for browsing and product assignment. Return validation errors for malformed input and 404 for missing categories.

responseBody.description: The updated category record after the administrator's changes are saved.

parameters.description: The category identifier (UUID) of the category to update.
parameters.name: categoryId

requestBody.description: Category fields to update, including the category name, description, and any permitted hierarchy-related fields supported by the category update model.

operations.description:
Delete a category that is managed by administrators.

This operation removes the category from the taxonomy used for browsing and organization. Products that were assigned to the deleted category must remain available and become uncategorized, so product browsing is preserved even after the category record is removed.

Only administrators may call this endpoint. Customers and sellers must be rejected. If the category does not exist, return a not-found error. If deleting the category would violate the validated one-level subcategory structure rules, reject the request before any data is changed.

Because this action affects catalog organization, the service should ensure category listings no longer include the deleted category after the transaction completes.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Verify the caller is an administrator before performing any database changes. Load the target category by its ID and confirm it exists.

Perform the deletion in a transaction. Remove the category record, then update all products that reference the deleted category so they no longer point to the removed taxonomy entry and are treated as uncategorized by browsing queries. Do not delete the products themselves, and do not alter product snapshots or other historical records.

If the category has dependent subcategory structure or any deletion would violate the one-level nesting constraints, abort without mutating data and return a validation error. If the category is missing, return 404. If the caller lacks permission, return 403.

Return no body on success, since clients can refresh category lists and product listings to reflect the deletion.

parameters.description: The category identifier to delete (global scope).
parameters.name: categoryId

operations.description:
Search and browse marketplace products with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

This operation returns customer-visible product listings across all sellers, including the results shown on search pages and category browsing pages. It supports keyword search, category filtering, minimum and maximum price filtering, in-stock-only filtering, and ordering options so clients can build consistent product discovery screens.

The response is paginated because product lists can exceed a single page. Products that are deleted or otherwise unavailable for browsing must not appear in the result set. Each summary item should contain the information needed for a listing card, including the main image, seller shop name, pricing summary, and average rating when reviews exist.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_products as the root catalog table for browsing.
Join related seller profile and product image data needed for customer-facing summaries, and include review aggregation data required for average rating and review count display.
Apply keyword search against product name, category filtering, minimum and maximum price filtering, and in-stock-only filtering according to the browsing rules. If the request targets a category that does not exist, reject the request.
Support sorting by newest first, price ascending, and price descending. Apply pagination consistently and return a page object containing product summaries only.
Exclude products that are deleted, hidden, suspended-seller owned, or otherwise unavailable for customer browsing. If a product has no available variants, it may still be returned only when the request does not require in-stock-only filtering, but its availability must be represented consistently in the summary data.

responseBody.description: Paginated marketplace product summaries for search and category browsing pages.

requestBody.description: Search, filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for browsing marketplace products.

operations.description:
Get a single product’s current catalog record.

This endpoint returns the live product entity used on product detail pages and by administrative oversight workflows. The product is the marketplace’s primary sellable listing, owned by a seller and optionally assigned to a category, so the response reflects the current browsing state of that listing.

The returned record includes the product’s stored fields: seller reference, category reference, name, description, base price, and timestamps. Related live data such as images, variants, and reviews may be included by the implementation when assembling the full entity response, but snapshot history is not the primary purpose of this route.

If the product does not exist or is no longer available, the operation should return a not-found error. This is a read-only endpoint and must not mutate any data.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_products by id and return the current live record. Validate the path parameter as a UUID and load the product from the active catalog table only; do not read from snapshot tables for this endpoint.

Use only actual schema columns: id, seller_account_id, category_id, name, description, base_price, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. If the record is missing or deleted, return not found. If the response assembler includes current images, variants, or reviews, it must respect the current live rows and exclude deleted rows according to the application’s read rules.

Keep the operation strictly read-only. Do not add pagination, filters, or update behavior to this route because it is a single-entity detail endpoint.

responseBody.description: The current live product record used for detail display.

parameters.description: The product identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Create a new marketplace product for the authenticated seller.

This operation lets an approved seller create a sellable product record with the required business identity fields. The new product is owned by the authenticated seller, assigned to the selected category, and then becomes available for later browsing, variant management, image management, and snapshot-based history tracking.

The product must include a name, description, category, and base price. The selected category may be a subcategory. The server must reject invalid category references and any request from a seller account that is not allowed to create products. If creation fails, no partial product data should be persisted.

Because products are the canonical browse and search entity, the created record becomes the source for product images, product variants, inventory records, order-item snapshots, and review presentation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate the authenticated actor as an approved seller with permission to create products.
Insert a new row into mall_platform_products using only fields defined by the product create DTO and the seller identity derived from authentication context.
Verify that the referenced category exists and can be assigned to a product, including subcategories.
Persist the product atomically; if any validation or persistence step fails, rollback the transaction and return an error without creating a partial record.
Do not create snapshots here; product snapshots are created only on later edits.
Return the full created product entity after insert so the client can navigate to the new product detail page. Ensure the response reflects the canonical product record and does not invent fields outside the schema.

responseBody.description: The newly created product record including its persisted identity and seller ownership context.

requestBody.description: Product creation data including the required product name, description, category, and base price.

operations.description:
Update an existing product owned by a seller.

This operation lets the owning seller modify the product's core catalog fields, including its name, description, category, and base price. The selected category may be a subcategory, and the product remains owned by the same seller account after the update.

When the update succeeds, the service must preserve the previous product state in a snapshot so the catalog history can be reviewed later for audit and dispute resolution. If the product does not exist, belongs to another seller, or is otherwise unavailable due to policy or account state restrictions, the request must fail with an appropriate business error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the product by product_id and verify it exists. Enforce that the caller is the owning seller unless the caller has administrator privileges for product oversight. Reject the operation if the product belongs to a seller account that is unavailable for business operations, or if the selected category does not exist.

Apply updates only to editable product fields: name, description, category_id, and base_price. Do not modify seller ownership, variants, inventory, orders, or snapshots directly in this operation. Persist the previous product state as a product snapshot before committing the update. The snapshot should capture the product data relevant to historical reconstruction, and the updated product must remain visible in browse/search flows according to its seller and category state.

Return the updated full product entity after persistence. If validation fails or the product cannot be updated, leave the product unchanged and do not create a snapshot. Use transactional handling so the snapshot write and product update succeed or fail together.

responseBody.description: The updated product after the change has been saved successfully.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product to update.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: The product fields to update, including the editable catalog attributes for the seller-owned product.

prerequisites.description: The referenced category must exist before the product can be assigned to it during the update.

operations.description:
Deletes a product from active marketplace listings.

This operation removes the specified product from customer browsing and search results when deletion is permitted by business rules. It is used by the product owner seller or by an administrator acting under policy enforcement. The deleted product itself is not physically erased from historical context; related snapshot records remain available for authorized review, and dependent catalog browsing behavior must continue to work for unaffected products.

Before deletion, the service must verify that the product has no pending order items in paid or shipped status for any of its variants, and no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant. If the product is deletable, all of its variants and their inventory records must also be removed from active use, and any wishlist references should stop pointing to the deleted product as part of the deletion flow.

If the product cannot be deleted because of active commercial dependencies, the API must reject the request with a conflict-style business error. If the product does not exist or is not accessible to the caller, the API must return a not-found or authorization-related error according to the platform's standard error handling rules.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target product by productId and verify that it exists.

Authorize the caller according to platform rules: the owning seller may delete their own product, and an administrator may delete any product for policy enforcement. Reject unauthorized callers.

Check all variants of the product for blocking dependencies before any deletion occurs. The product may only be deleted when none of its variants have pending order items with paid or shipped status, and none of its variants have pending cancellation or refund requests. If any blocking dependency exists, abort the operation with a conflict error and do not modify the database.

When deletion is allowed, execute the removal in a transaction. Delete all product variants, remove their inventory records from active use, and delete the product record itself. Ensure any ancillary active references that depend on the product being present are cleaned up as part of the service flow, while historical snapshot records remain untouched. The product must no longer appear in search or category browsing after completion.

Return the deleted product entity if the implementation supports echoing the removed record; otherwise return no content. All error responses must be consistent with the platform's standard not-found, forbidden, and conflict semantics.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product to delete (UUID scope).
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Returns a paginated list of marketplace products for browsing and search.

This operation supports the customer-facing catalog experience, including search results and category browsing. It returns product summaries only, with filtering and sorting applied before pagination so that the result set reflects the selected browsing criteria.

The response excludes products that are not eligible for catalog visibility, such as deleted products or products from unavailable seller states. Products with no variants may still be returned as unavailable rather than purchasable. If no products match the query, the response contains an empty page instead of an error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_products as the primary catalog source and build a paginated summary result for browsing. Apply search text, category filter, minimum price, maximum price, in-stock-only filtering, and sort order in the database query or service query pipeline.

Validate any requested category filter against mall_platform_categories before executing the product query. Exclude products that are not visible for browsing due to deleted state or seller availability restrictions. Derive summary fields from the product record and related data such as the main image, seller shop name, price display, and average rating. Preserve stable ordering for pagination and return an empty page when nothing matches.

responseBody.description: Paginated marketplace product summaries for browsing and search results.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for browsing marketplace products.

operations.description:
List the preserved snapshot history for a specific product.

This endpoint returns immutable product snapshots so the owning seller and administrators can review earlier product states for disputes, policy checks, and historical inspection. Product snapshots remain available even after the active product has been deleted, and each snapshot represents the product state that existed when the snapshot was recorded.

The records are scoped to the product identified by `productId`. Access is limited to the product owner and administrators. If the product does not exist or the caller is not authorized to view its history, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found or forbidden response. Snapshot data is read-only and must never be modified through this API.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the product by `productId`, then verify that the caller is either the owning seller or an administrator before querying snapshot history. Read the immutable snapshot rows for that product and return them in descending chronological order, using the snapshot timestamp or stored creation order.

Support pagination and any allowed list filters through the request body. Do not expose mutation behavior, and do not attempt to reconstruct historical values from the live product once a snapshot exists; the snapshot table is the source of truth. Preserve access after product deletion, since historical snapshots must remain available for review. Return an empty page when no snapshots exist.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product snapshot summaries for the specified product.

parameters.description: The UUID of the product whose snapshot history should be listed.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Search and paging criteria for the product snapshot list, including pagination, sorting, and any permitted historical filters.

operations.description:
Retrieve one immutable snapshot of a product's preserved historical state.

This operation returns the full snapshot record for a specific product, including the product data captured at that moment and the preserved image and variant state required for later dispute review or historical inspection. It is intended for the product owner and administrators, who are allowed to view snapshots even when the active product has already changed or been deleted.

The snapshot is scoped by both `productId` and `snapshotId`, and the snapshot must belong to the specified product. If the snapshot does not exist, belongs to another product, or the caller is not authorized to view it, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found or forbidden response according to the platform's access rules. Because snapshots are immutable, this endpoint never modifies data.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the product snapshot by `snapshotId` and verify that it is associated with `productId` before returning it. Read the preserved snapshot record and any related preserved image/variant snapshot rows needed to construct the complete historical view. Do not substitute the current product record; the response must reflect the exact preserved state stored in the snapshot.

Authorize access for the owning seller and administrators only. If the active product has been deleted, the snapshot remains retrievable when the caller has permission. The endpoint is strictly read-only and must not create, update, or delete any rows. Return not-found when the snapshot cannot be located or does not belong to the given product, and forbidden when the caller lacks access.

responseBody.description: The preserved product snapshot, including the full historical product state captured when the snapshot was created.

operations.description:
Returns a paginated list of variants for one product.

This endpoint is used to inspect the product’s purchasable variants in a seller-facing management view. Each item summarizes the variant’s SKU code, option values, optional price override, and current availability-related state derived from stock context.

The product identifier is required because variants belong to exactly one product. The endpoint supports search, pagination, and sorting so clients can work with large variant sets. If the product does not exist, the request should return a not found error. If the caller is not allowed to access the product, the request should return a forbidden error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the parent product by productId first, then query mall_platform_product_variants constrained to that product. Apply request filters, pagination, and sorting only within the product scope. Return summary rows only; do not expand full inventory history, snapshots, or unrelated product data.

The service must not return variants from other products. If the product is missing, return not found. If access is denied, return forbidden. Validate request pagination and search parameters before querying. The summary should be derived from the current database state, including SKU code, option values, optional price override, and variant availability derived from inventory state.

operations.description:
Create a new purchasable variant for a product.

This operation lets the owning seller add a SKU-identified variation to an existing product, such as a specific color and size combination. The variant belongs to the product identified by the path parameter and becomes part of the product's sellable options after it is created successfully.

The service must verify that the product exists and that the authenticated seller owns it. It must reject requests that try to create a duplicate SKU code, because variant SKU codes must be unique across the platform. Validation should also ensure that the variant payload includes the required option values and any other required fields defined by the variant create contract.

If the product cannot be modified because it does not exist, the request should return not found. If the authenticated seller does not own the product, it should return forbidden. If the SKU already exists, it should return a conflict or validation error. The creation should be transactional so that no partial variant data is persisted when validation fails.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target product by productId and confirm it exists. Verify the authenticated seller owns the product and is allowed to modify it.

Validate the create payload using the product variant creation contract. Require the SKU code and option values, and support an optional variant price override if allowed by the domain model. Enforce SKU uniqueness at the application or database level before insert.

Insert the new variant linked to the product. The request body must not repeat productId because the route already provides the parent scope. Return the created variant record after persistence.

Handle errors as follows: not found when the product does not exist, forbidden when the seller does not own the product, and conflict or validation failure when the SKU code is already used. Keep the operation transactional to prevent partial writes.

This endpoint returns the full variant record for the specified product and variant pair so clients can display SKU-level details such as option values, pricing, and availability. The product scope ensures the variant belongs to the requested product and prevents cross-product ambiguity.

If the product does not exist, the variant does not exist, or the variant does not belong to the specified product, the server should return a not-found response. This operation is read-only and does not modify inventory, product data, or snapshot history.
operations.name: at

Prefer a single query that joins or filters by both identifiers to avoid cross-product leakage. If separate lookups are required, return 404 when the product is missing, when the variant is missing, or when the ownership relationship does not match. Do not expose variants from other products.

Return the canonical product variant entity shape from mall_platform_product_variants, including the persisted fields needed by the UI and downstream business logic such as SKU code, option combination, optional price override, and availability state. Do not invent fields that are not in the schema, and do not create or modify inventory records in this operation.

operations.description:
Updates a single product variant within the specified product.

This operation lets the product owner edit a variant's SKU code, option values, pricing override, and availability-related data while keeping the variant tied to its parent product. Both identifiers are required so the server can confirm that the variant belongs to the specified product before applying changes.

The server must reject requests for missing records, cross-product variant references, unauthorized callers, and duplicate SKU codes. Because variant edits are part of the marketplace's auditable pricing and inventory-sensitive history, the implementation should preserve the previous state in a snapshot before committing the update.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the parent product by productId and verify the variant belongs to it. Reject the request if either record is missing or if the caller is not the owning seller or an administrator with product oversight privileges.

Validate the update payload against the product variant model. Enforce global uniqueness of skuCode across mall_platform_product_variants, excluding the current variant row. Apply any option-value constraints required by the domain model and ensure price override updates remain valid for the product's pricing rules.

Before persisting the change, insert a variant snapshot capturing the previous variant state so historical review and dispute workflows can reconstruct what changed. Execute the snapshot write and the variant update inside one transaction. If variant option rows are normalized into a child table, synchronize them in the same transaction.

Return the updated variant after commit. Surface uniqueness conflicts, authorization failures, and concurrent modification issues as appropriate errors, and do not allow partial updates if any step fails.

responseBody.description: The updated product variant after the change has been saved.
