operations.description:
Deletes a product variant that belongs to the specified product.

This operation removes one purchasable variant from a seller-owned product. It is only allowed when the variant is no longer needed for active order processing or dispute handling. If the deleted variant was the last remaining variant for the product, the product becomes unavailable for future purchase selection, although it may still remain visible according to normal catalog rules.

The deletion is restricted to the product owner or an administrator, depending on the platform authorization policy. The operation must reject requests when the product or variant does not exist, when the variant does not belong to the specified product, or when pending paid/shipped order items, cancellation requests, or refund requests still reference the variant.

Historical records and snapshots must remain preserved for audit and dispute review. The deletion only affects the active variant record and its active availability in the catalog.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the product and variant using both path identifiers and verify that the variant belongs to the specified product.
Check authorization so only the product owner or an administrator can perform the deletion.
Before deleting, verify that no order items for the variant are still pending in paid or shipped status, and that no pending cancellation requests or refund requests exist for the variant.
If any blocker exists, reject the request with a conflict-style business error and do not remove the record.
If the variant is the last active variant for the product, mark the product as unavailable for purchase by virtue of having no purchasable variants remaining.
Delete only the active variant record; preserve snapshots and historical records intact.
Return success with no response body when deletion completes.

parameters.description: The identifier of the product that owns the variant.
parameters.name: productId

parameters.description: The identifier of the variant to delete within the specified product.

operations.description:
Reorder the images attached to a product.

This operation updates the seller-managed image collection for a single product. The submitted order determines how the images appear on the product detail page, and the first image becomes the main thumbnail used in listings and search results.

Only the seller who owns the product may perform this action. If any referenced image is unavailable, does not belong to the product, or the requested order is invalid, the system must reject the update without changing the current image set. When the reorder succeeds, the change must be preserved in the product snapshot history so the previous and updated image order can be reviewed later for dispute resolution.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target product by productId and verify that the authenticated seller owns it and is permitted to maintain its images. Interpret the request body as a full reorder of the product image set, not a partial update.

Validate that the requested image sequence contains only images that belong to the product, that no image is missing or duplicated, and that every referenced image is currently available. Update the stored ordering atomically so the first image becomes the thumbnail image used by product listings.

After a successful reorder, create the corresponding product snapshot entry to preserve the prior and updated image state together with the product's other editable data. If validation fails, leave the image order unchanged and do not create a snapshot. Return business errors for missing product, unauthorized seller, unavailable image target, or invalid ordering.

responseBody.description: A paginated summary of the product images after the reorder has been applied, so the client can refresh the visual presentation state.

parameters.description: The product identifier whose image order is being updated.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: The desired final order of the product images. The order of the submitted items determines the gallery order, and the first item becomes the product thumbnail.

Attach a new image to a product.

This operation lets the owning seller add a presentation image to the specified product so it appears in listings and on the product detail page. The new image becomes part of the product's ordered gallery, and its position affects which image is used as the main thumbnail.

Only the seller who owns the product may perform this action. The service must verify that the product exists and that the authenticated seller is allowed to maintain it before creating the image. If the product is unavailable or the caller is not the owner, the request must fail without changing any existing images.

After the image is created, the system must preserve the updated image order and record the change in the product history through a snapshot. The response returns the newly created product image with its current ordering state.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Fetch the target product by productId and confirm it belongs to the authenticated seller. Reject the request if the product does not exist or if the caller lacks ownership rights for product maintenance.

Insert a mall_platform_product_images row associated with that product using the request body fields. If the create DTO includes an ordering field, insert the image at the requested position and shift later images consistently in the same transaction; otherwise append it to the end of the product's image set.

After insertion, create the corresponding product image snapshot so the visual history remains traceable. Do not alter unrelated products or image sets. Roll back the transaction on any validation or persistence error and return the appropriate business error.

This operation is used by the seller who owns the product to maintain the product's visual presentation. The product image list is ordered, so any successful change must preserve the sequence that determines the main thumbnail image shown in listings and the display order on the product detail page.

The request is rejected when the product does not exist, the image does not belong to the specified product, or the caller is not the owning seller. If the update changes ordering-related data, the system must keep the image set consistent and must not alter unrelated images. Every successful update is recorded in snapshot history so past product presentation can be reviewed later.

Fetch the product by productId and the image by imageId, then confirm the image belongs to that product and that the authenticated seller owns the product. Reject the request if the product is missing, the image is missing, ownership does not match, or the product is not available for maintenance.

Apply only the mutable fields defined by the product image schema. If the payload affects ordering, recompute the product's image ordering in a transaction so the first image remains the thumbnail image and other images keep a stable relative order unless explicitly changed. Do not reorder or delete unrelated images when the target image is unavailable.

Before committing the update, create the required snapshot entry capturing the prior image state and any order-sensitive state needed for audit history. Return the updated image after the transaction succeeds. If any validation or persistence step fails, roll back the entire change.

Delete one image from a product's ordered image set.

This operation removes the specified image from the product that the authenticated seller owns. If the deleted image was the first image, the next remaining image becomes the new main thumbnail image. If it was the only image, the product remains without a thumbnail until a new image is added.

The product must exist, must still be manageable, and the target image must belong to that product. If the product is unavailable, the seller does not own the product, or the image no longer exists, the request is rejected and no other images are changed. The deletion is preserved in the product image history used for dispute review and visual reconstruction.

After deletion, recompute or renumber the remaining images so the first image remains the thumbnail candidate and the display order stays contiguous. If the deleted image was the only image, leave the product with no thumbnail until another image is added.

Do not change unrelated images, variants, or product fields. Record the change through the product image snapshot/history mechanism so prior presentation state remains traceable. Return no response body for a successful delete unless the platform contract requires one.

operations.description:
List the inventory movement history for a specific product variant.

This endpoint returns the append-only inventory records associated with one variant under one product. It is intended for seller-side auditing and stock review, showing the quantity change, recorded reason, and creation timestamp for each inventory movement.

The request is scoped by both product and variant so the history can only be read for the correct product-variant pair. If the product does not exist, the variant does not exist, or the variant does not belong to the specified product, the request must return a not-found error.

Results are paginated and can be filtered or sorted according to the request body. Because inventory records are history entries rather than editable resources, this operation is read-only and has no side effects.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Verify that the product exists and that the variant belongs to that product before querying history. Query mall_platform_inventory_records by the variant foreign key, then apply pagination, filtering, and sorting from IMallPlatformInventoryRecord.IRequest. Default sorting should favor the most recent records first unless the request explicitly asks for another supported order.

Do not calculate or mutate current stock here; current stock is derived elsewhere by summing inventory records. Preserve append-only semantics by exposing read access only. If authorization restricts history viewing to sellers or owners, enforce that before the query. Return not found when the product-variant relationship is invalid, even if one identifier exists.

The variant must belong to the product identified in the path, and the caller must be authorized to manage that product's inventory. If the product or variant does not exist, or if the variant is not owned by the product, the request must fail. If the inventory change cannot be applied, the system must leave the existing stock unchanged and return an error without creating a partial update.

Validate all business constraints before persisting the record, including product/variant scope and any stock rules imposed by the inventory adjustment type. If any validation or persistence step fails, roll back the transaction so no partial stock change is applied and the historical sequence remains consistent.

Return the created inventory record in the response body for immediate confirmation and history display.

This endpoint returns preserved historical records for the selected variant so the owning seller or an administrator can review how the variant changed over time. Snapshot records remain available even if the live product or variant has been edited or deleted, and they are intended for audit review, dispute resolution, and change history inspection.

The service must verify that the variant belongs to the specified product before querying snapshots. If the product or variant does not exist, or if the variant is not associated with the product, return a not found error. Access is limited to the product owner seller and administrators.

Because snapshots are immutable, do not implement create, update, or delete behavior here. Return an empty page when no snapshots match. Return a not found error when the product or variant is missing, or when the relationship between them is invalid. Enforce authorization so only the owning seller and administrators can access the results.

Retrieve one immutable snapshot of a product variant.

This operation returns the preserved historical state of a single variant for audit, dispute resolution, and review of prior edits. It is read-only and does not affect the current product, variant, inventory, or pricing data.

The snapshot is scoped to the specified product and variant, so the service must verify that the variant belongs to the product and that the snapshot belongs to that variant before returning data. If the relationship chain is invalid or the caller is not allowed to view the snapshot, the service should return an appropriate not-found or forbidden response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the snapshot by traversing the ownership chain from product to variant to snapshot. First confirm that the variant belongs to the specified product, then confirm that the snapshot belongs to that variant. Return the immutable snapshot record only.

Authorize access so the owning seller can view snapshots of their own product variants and administrators can view any snapshot. If any identifier does not match the expected ownership chain, return not found rather than exposing broader data. Do not modify any current state or create any new records.

Use the full product variant snapshot DTO in the response. The DTO should represent the preserved variant state needed for historical inspection and should not include request-only fields or mutable current-state references.

operations.description:
Returns the normalized option-value records captured for one product variant snapshot.

This operation is intended for read-only historical inspection of a variant's option state at the moment the snapshot was created. It is useful for audit review, dispute handling, and reconstruction of the exact variant configuration that existed before later edits.

The snapshot is strictly scoped to a product, one of its variants, and that variant's snapshot. The server must verify that the product owns the variant and that the variant owns the snapshot before reading any option rows. If the scope does not match, the request must fail with a not-found response to avoid exposing historical data from another product tree.

The response is paginated because a snapshot can contain multiple option-value pairs. Consumers can filter, sort, and page through the snapshot options using the request body, but they cannot modify any snapshot content through this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Validate the hierarchy first: productId must own variantId, and variantId must own snapshotId. Reject invalid scope combinations with 404.
Query mall_platform_product_variant_snapshot_options by snapshot identifier, applying the request body's search, pagination, and sorting rules. Return only immutable historical rows; do not expose current variant state or attempt any mutation.
Because the endpoint is a list/search operation, keep it as PATCH and return a paginated summary model. If the request attempts unsupported filters or sorts, apply the platform's standard validation errors. The implementation should be efficient for large snapshots and should not load unrelated snapshots or products.

operations.description:
Return the authenticated customer's current shopping cart for purchase review.

The response shows the active cart so the customer can inspect selected product variants, quantities, item subtotals, and the cart total before checkout. Unavailable or low-stock items remain visible so the customer can resolve them without losing the rest of the cart.

The cart is resolved from the authenticated customer session and must never expose another customer's data. The response should reflect the current cart state and support the buyer flow that continues into checkout and order placement.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the current customer from the authenticated session and load that customer's shopping cart header together with all related cart items.
Include the product and product-variant data needed to render product name, variant options, unit price, quantity, item subtotal, and availability state.
Show unavailable items when the underlying variant has been deleted, is out of stock, or is otherwise not purchasable so the customer can correct the cart before checkout.
Compute each item subtotal from the stored unit price and quantity, and compute the cart total as the sum of all item subtotals. Do not mutate cart data during this read operation.
If the customer has no cart record, follow the application's cart initialization policy consistently: either return an empty cart representation or the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
Scope the query strictly to the current customer account and prevent any cross-user data leakage.

responseBody.description: The authenticated customer's shopping cart with line items and summary pricing for purchase review.

operations.description:
Update one or more quantities in the authenticated customer’s shopping cart.

Each cart item remains tied to the same product variant; this endpoint only changes the selected quantity and does not reassign the line to a different variant. If the same variant is already present in the cart, the quantities must be combined according to cart rules rather than split into duplicate lines.

The service must verify cart ownership, reject invalid quantities, and preserve the cart unchanged when validation fails. If requested quantities exceed available stock, the line may remain in the cart with a stock warning instead of being silently truncated. After a successful update, the cart item subtotal and cart total must be recalculated from the persisted quantities.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated customer’s shopping cart, locate the target cart item(s), and update quantities atomically within one transaction.

Confirm that every referenced cart item belongs to the current customer and still points to a valid product variant. Do not permit any request to change the variant reference itself; only quantity may change. Validate that quantities are positive integers and that any business-specific cart rules are satisfied before persisting changes.

If a requested quantity exceeds available stock, keep the cart line and expose the stock-warning state required by cart rules. If any item fails authorization, validation, or existence checks, abort the entire operation without committing partial changes. Recompute affected line subtotals and the overall cart total after persistence, then return the refreshed paginated cart summary representation for the client.

responseBody.description: Paginated shopping cart summary data reflecting the authenticated customer’s cart after the quantity update has been applied.

requestBody.description: Request payload for changing the quantity of one or more cart items in the authenticated customer’s shopping cart.

operations.description:
Adds a product variant to the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

The operation creates a cart line for one specific variant and combines the quantity with an existing line when that variant is already present. The cart stores variant selections rather than product-level selections, so the request must identify the exact purchasable variant and the desired quantity.

The server validates ownership, variant availability, and quantity rules before applying the change. If the variant is deleted, unavailable, or cannot be added, the request is rejected without changing the cart. If the resulting quantity exceeds available stock, the cart item may remain in the cart for review, but the operation must still enforce the platform's quantity validation rules.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated customer and load their shopping cart.
Load the target product variant and verify that it exists and is available for purchase.
Validate that the requested quantity is a positive integer.
If a cart item for the same variant already exists in the cart, update that row by adding the new quantity to the existing quantity instead of inserting a duplicate.
Perform the add-or-merge logic in a transaction so the cart remains consistent if a validation or persistence error occurs.
If the variant is out of stock or otherwise unavailable, reject the request with a business error and leave the cart unchanged.
Return the persisted cart item after the change so the client can refresh the cart display.

responseBody.description: The shopping cart item created or updated by this operation.

requestBody.description: Details for the selected product variant and quantity to add to the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

operations.description:
Update a cart item quantity in the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

This endpoint changes the purchase amount for an existing product-variant line while keeping the same variant association. The service must recalculate the cart item subtotal and any cart-level totals after the update, and it must preserve the item in the cart even when the quantity exceeds available stock so the client can show a stock warning.

The operation must verify that the cart item belongs to the current customer before applying changes. If the cart item does not exist, is not owned by the caller, or the requested quantity violates cart rules, the service must reject the request without partially changing the cart.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target cart item by cartItemId and confirm ownership through the parent shopping cart for the authenticated customer.
Update only mutable fields in mall_platform_cart_items; this endpoint must not change the selected product variant.
Validate the requested quantity as a positive purchase amount. If the same variant is already represented by another line, combine quantities into the existing line instead of creating a duplicate.
Recompute the cart item subtotal and any dependent cart summary values using the current variant pricing and the final quantity.
If the requested quantity exceeds available stock, persist the quantity and leave the item eligible for warning display rather than rejecting it outright.
Return 404 when the cart item is missing or not owned by the caller, and return 422 for invalid quantity or other cart-rule violations. Perform the update transactionally so a failure does not leave the cart item partially changed.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item after quantity and subtotal recalculation.

parameters.description: The cart item identifier within the authenticated customer's shopping cart.
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: The editable cart item fields, primarily the quantity for the selected variant line.

operations.description:
Remove one item from the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

This operation deletes a cart line that references a specific product variant and recalculates the cart total after removal. If the cart item does not exist, the request has no effect and still succeeds, matching the cart removal business rule.

The operation only affects the current customer's shopping cart data. It does not change the underlying product, variant, inventory, or order records.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Locate the cart item by cartItemId and confirm it belongs to the authenticated customer through the owning shopping cart. If the item exists, delete the row from mall_platform_cart_items and update any derived cart total used by the cart aggregate. If the item is already missing, return success without modifying data.

Do not mutate product, variant, inventory, or order tables. Do not accept a request body. Enforce ownership so a customer cannot remove another customer's cart item. Return an empty successful response on completion.

parameters.description: The identifier of the cart item to remove from the authenticated customer's cart.
parameters.name: cartItemId

operations.description:
Returns the authenticated customer's wishlist as a paginated list of saved products.

This endpoint is used to browse products the customer saved for later consideration. It returns product-level wishlist entries only, not variant-level rows, and the result is limited to the caller's own wishlist. Deleted products must not appear in the response because wishlist maintenance keeps saved items aligned with products that still exist in the catalog.

Pagination is required so customers can browse large saved-product lists in manageable groups. If the customer is not authenticated or does not own a wishlist, the request must be rejected by the authorization layer.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the current customer from the authenticated session, load that customer's wishlist container, and query wishlist items joined to the current product records used for browsing. Exclude wishlist entries whose referenced product no longer exists so deleted products do not surface in the list. Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request body, and return only product-level summary data suitable for a wishlist view.

Do not expose variant-level fields in this operation. The list must be scoped to the authenticated customer only, and cross-customer access is prohibited. If the customer is unauthenticated, return an authorization failure. If the wishlist container cannot be found for the authenticated customer, return the standard not-found behavior for that scope. This endpoint is read-only and must not modify wishlist rows.

responseBody.description: Paginated wishlist browsing results containing the customer's saved products.

requestBody.description: Wishlist browsing criteria including pagination, optional product search filters, and sorting options for the authenticated customer's saved products.

operations.description:
Returns the authenticated customer's wishlist entries as a paginated list of saved products.

This endpoint is limited to the caller's own wishlist and each entry represents a product, not a variant. Deleted products must be excluded from the returned list so wishlist browsing always reflects catalog items that still exist.

Use this endpoint for customer wishlist browsing, search, and sorting. The response is intended for list presentation and does not expose other customers' wishlist data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated customer's wishlist container and return wishlist items whose linked products still exist in the catalog. Filter out any entries whose product has been deleted, and never return another customer's data.

Support pagination, keyword search, and sorting in the request body. Search and sort should operate on product-facing fields only. If the customer has no wishlist or no valid wishlist items remain, return an empty page.

This endpoint is read-only and must not create, update, or delete wishlist records.

responseBody.description: Paginated wishlist item summaries for the authenticated customer, containing only active products that remain in the catalog.

requestBody.description: Wishlist browsing criteria including pagination, keyword search, and sorting options for the current customer's saved products.

operations.description:
Save a product to the current customer's wishlist.

This operation creates a single wishlist entry at product level so customers can keep products for later without selecting a specific variant. The wishlist belongs to the authenticated customer account, and ownership must be resolved from the session rather than supplied by the client.

The service must verify that the referenced product exists, is still available, and is not already saved by the same customer. Duplicate wishlist entries for the same customer and product should be rejected. If the product has been deleted, the request must fail and the customer's existing wishlist contents must remain unchanged.

On success, the created wishlist item is returned for immediate UI refresh.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the current customer from authentication, then locate or validate the customer's wishlist container. Accept only the product reference from the request body and ignore any ownership fields that may be present in downstream DTOs.

Validate that the product exists in the products table and is eligible to be wishlisted. Enforce one product per customer wishlist item, preferably with a unique constraint on wishlist_id and product_id to protect against concurrent duplicate requests. Convert duplicate-key violations into a conflict response.

Insert the wishlist item only after all validations pass. Do not store variant references, quantities, pricing, or any cart-related data. If the product cannot be found, has been deleted, or the insert fails, return an error without changing the customer's saved items.

responseBody.description: The newly created wishlist item for the current customer.

requestBody.description: Data needed to save one product in the authenticated customer's wishlist.

operations.description:
Removes one saved product entry from the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This endpoint deletes a single wishlist item and leaves the underlying product record unchanged. It only affects the saved item row in the wishlist data and does not modify the wishlist container or any other saved products.

If the specified wishlist item does not exist, the request should still succeed without changing any data so repeated delete calls remain safe. If the item belongs to a different customer, the service must reject the request using the platform's standard ownership or authorization failure behavior.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Look up the wishlist item by wishlistItemId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer through the owning wishlist relationship. If the item is missing, return success without side effects so the delete operation is idempotent.

If the item exists and belongs to the current customer, delete only that row from mall_platform_wishlist_items. Do not delete the wishlist container, do not alter the product record, and do not touch other wishlist items. If the item has already become stale because the product was deleted, the same delete path should still safely remove the row if present or no-op if it has already been cleaned up.

Reject cross-account deletion attempts according to the service's standard forbidden or not-found policy for ownership violations.

parameters.description: The identifier of the wishlist item to remove from the authenticated customer's wishlist.
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

operations.description:
List the authenticated customer's orders with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

This endpoint returns the current customer's order history only. It is intended for browsing past purchases, checking the derived overall order status, and navigating to a separate order detail view when more information is needed. The overall status shown in the list is derived from the statuses of the order items, so the list reflects the platform's order-state rules.

The request body supports the browsing criteria defined for orders, including pagination and any allowed filters or sort options. Results must be ordered according to the requested sort, with a sensible default of newest first. The service must reject attempts to access other customers' orders and must not mutate any order data.

If invalid pagination or unsupported criteria are supplied, the request should fail with a business validation error. Full item details, shipment details, and preserved snapshot information belong to the order detail endpoint rather than this list endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_orders for the authenticated customer only.
Apply request-body filters and sorting for the order browsing use case, then paginate the result set.
Return a summary projection suitable for list pages, including order identity, date, total price, and the overall status derived from mall_platform_order_items according to the order status rules.
Do not include full item rows, shipment details, or snapshot payloads in the list response.
Reject unauthorized cross-account access. Validate paging and filter criteria before querying, and return a business error if the request is invalid.

responseBody.description: Paginated order summaries for the authenticated customer, including the derived overall status and other list-friendly order fields.

requestBody.description: Filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for the authenticated customer's order history.

operations.description:
Returns the full detail view of one order owned by the current customer.

This endpoint is used from the customer order history flow to open a single order and inspect its complete purchase record. The response includes the order header, shipping destination, item-level purchase history, and shipment information needed to understand progress at both the order and order-item level.

Access is restricted to the authenticated customer who owns the order. If the order does not exist or does not belong to the current customer, the service must respond as not found to avoid exposing another customer's purchase history. The order's preserved historical item information must remain intact even if seller profiles or product data change later.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the order by primary key and verify that the authenticated customer owns it before returning data. Join the order with its order items, preserved order-item snapshot data, shipping address, and any shipments/items associated with the order so the detail page can render the full history.

Return the preserved item-level purchase context exactly as stored at checkout time, including product and variant references captured in the order item snapshots, rather than resolving only current catalog data. Include shipment tracking data when present, and ensure the response remains stable even if the seller profile, product, or variant has since changed.

If the order is missing or belongs to another customer, return a not found response. Do not leak whether another customer's order exists. Do not allow modification through this endpoint.

responseBody.description: Full order detail for the authenticated customer, including order items, preserved purchase context, shipping address, and shipment tracking data.

parameters.description: The order identifier (UUID).
parameters.name: orderId

operations.description:
Search and page through order items for operational workflows.

This endpoint returns live order item records so sellers and administrators can inspect purchased variant lines, fulfillment status, and request-related states in a paginated list. It is intended for collection browsing, status monitoring, and workflow triage rather than full record retrieval.

The search can be filtered by order, seller, product variant, and item status, and it should support stable sorting with newest items first by default. If no rows match the criteria, the endpoint should return an empty page. Deleted rows must be handled consistently with platform browsing rules and should not alter stored order history.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_order_items with pagination, filtering, and sorting support.
Use mall_platform_order_id, mall_platform_seller_id, mall_platform_product_variant_id, and status as supported filters.
Apply a deterministic sort order, defaulting to created_at descending when the request does not specify otherwise.
Return a paginated summary projection for list views; do not expose the entire order item entity in the collection payload.
Leverage the existing indexes on (mall_platform_order_id, status), (mall_platform_seller_id, status), and (mall_platform_product_variant_id, status) for efficient filtering.
If the requested page is beyond the available range or no rows match, return an empty page instead of an error.

responseBody.description: Paginated order item summaries for operational browsing and status monitoring.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for paging, filtering, and sorting order items by order, seller, product variant, and status.

operations.description:
Retrieve one order item together with its purchase context and current status.

This operation returns a single line item from a completed order. It is used for customer order history, seller fulfillment screens, shipment review, cancellation and refund handling, and administrator dispute review. The order item must remain scoped to its parent order and its preserved historical purchase data.

The response should expose the item’s quantity, item status, purchased product and variant references, seller context, and any preserved snapshot-based history required to understand the line item at the time of purchase. If the item does not exist, the service should return a standard not-found error. Access control must ensure that customers can only read their own order items, sellers can only read items related to their products, and administrators can read any order item.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the order item by its identifier and return the full detail representation for the line item. Use the order items table as the source of truth for the current state, and include any preserved purchase-context fields needed by the application layer for product, variant, seller, and status history.

Authorize the request before returning data: the owning customer may view the item, the seller associated with the item may view it, and administrators may view any item. If the row is missing, return a standard not-found response. Do not return sibling order items or mutate any data.

Keep the response aligned with the current persisted state and preserve snapshot-derived historical context where the system stores it for later review.

responseBody.description: The full order item record for the requested identifier, including its current state and preserved purchase context.

parameters.description: The order item identifier to retrieve.
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve the immutable snapshot history for a single order item.

This endpoint returns preserved historical records for the specified order item so the customer, the seller, and administrators can review how the item changed over time. The snapshots are read-only and remain available for audit and dispute resolution even if the source order item or related active records are later removed.

The request is scoped by the order item identifier in the path. Clients can page through the history and sort the results to inspect the sequence of preserved states without changing any stored data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the order item snapshot records filtered by orderItemId, then apply pagination, sorting, and any allowed search criteria supplied in the request body. Return newest-first ordering by default unless the request explicitly specifies another sort order.

Never modify snapshot rows because they are immutable. If the order item does not exist, return a not-found error. If the authenticated user is not allowed to view snapshots for this order item, return a forbidden error. If there are no snapshots, return an empty page. Include the preserved summary data needed for historical review, but do not attempt to reconstruct or alter active order item state.

responseBody.description: Paginated immutable snapshot records for the specified order item, suitable for audit and historical review.

parameters.description: The order item identifier whose snapshot history is being requested.
parameters.name: orderItemId

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for the order item snapshot history.

operations.description:
Retrieve the immutable snapshot history for a single order item.

This endpoint returns preserved historical records for the specified order item so the customer, the seller, and administrators can review how the item changed over time. The snapshots are read-only and remain available for audit and dispute resolution even if the source order item or related active records are later removed.

The request is scoped by the order item identifier in the path. Clients can page through the history and sort the results to inspect the sequence of preserved states without changing any stored data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the order item snapshot records filtered by orderItemId, then apply pagination, sorting, and any allowed search criteria supplied in the request body. Return newest-first ordering by default unless the request explicitly specifies another sort order.

Never modify snapshot rows because they are immutable. If the order item does not exist, return a not-found error. If the authenticated user is not allowed to view snapshots for this order item, return a forbidden error. If there are no snapshots, return an empty page. Include the preserved summary data needed for historical review, but do not attempt to reconstruct or alter active order item state.

responseBody.description: Paginated immutable snapshot records for the specified order item, suitable for audit and historical review.

parameters.description: The order item identifier whose snapshot history is being requested.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for the order item snapshot history.

The request is scoped by the order item identifier in the path. Clients can page through the history and sort the results to inspect the sequence of preserved states without changing any stored data.

operations.specification:

If the authenticated user is not allowed to view snapshots for this order item, return a forbidden error. If there are no snapshots, return an empty page. Include the preserved summary data needed for historical review, but do not attempt to reconstruct or alter active order item state.

operations.description:
Retrieve one immutable order item snapshot for historical purchase review.

This endpoint returns the preserved state of an order item at the time the snapshot was created. It is used for order history, dispute resolution, and reconstruction of the original purchase context even if the live order item, product, variant, or seller profile has changed or been deleted later.

The snapshot cannot be modified or deleted through this API. Access should be restricted to users who are allowed to inspect preserved order history, including the purchasing customer, the selling party, and administrators. If the specified order item does not exist, the snapshot does not exist, or the snapshot does not belong to the specified order item, the service should return not found.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Validate the parent order item ID and snapshot ID together so the snapshot is only returned when it belongs to the requested order item. Use a single read path that joins or otherwise verifies the parent-child relationship before returning data.

Return the full immutable snapshot record, including preserved purchase context and any normalized child data required by the snapshot model, such as stored option rows. Do not recompute snapshot values from current product or seller data. Do not allow updates or deletes through this endpoint. If the snapshot is missing or mismatched to the parent order item, return not found. Enforce the platform's access rules for preserved order history before returning the record.

responseBody.description: The full immutable order item snapshot, including preserved product, variant, seller profile, and purchase context.

operations.description:
Browse the preserved variant option rows for a specific order item snapshot.

This operation returns the normalized option-value pairs captured when the order item snapshot was created. It is intended for historical review, audit, and dispute handling, and it must reflect the immutable snapshot state exactly as stored.

The response is scoped to the given order item and snapshot identifiers. If the snapshot cannot be found, the service should return the standard not-found response for the scoped historical record. When the snapshot contains multiple option rows, the result must be paginated and sorted deterministically so the preserved state can be reviewed consistently.

operations.description:
Retrieve one preserved variant option row from an order item snapshot.

This endpoint returns a single atomic option-name and option-value pair captured as part of a historical order item snapshot. The record is only meaningful in the context of its parent order item and its snapshot, because it represents one piece of the purchased variant configuration preserved for audit and dispute review.

The data is immutable and is used to reconstruct what the customer actually bought at purchase time. If the requested option does not belong to the supplied order item snapshot, the request must return not found.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch a single mall_platform_order_item_snapshot_variant_options row by id and verify that it belongs to the supplied mall_platform_order_item_snapshots record, which must belong to the supplied mall_platform_order_items record. Use the three path parameters as strict ownership and scope checks before returning data.

Return the persisted fields from the row: id, mall_platform_order_item_snapshot_id, option_name, option_value, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Do not attempt any mutation or derived rewriting because this table stores historical snapshot data. If the parent-child chain does not match the supplied ids, return not found rather than exposing unrelated historical data.

responseBody.description: The preserved variant option record for the requested order item snapshot.

operations.description:
Search and browse shipments in a paginated list.

Shipments are seller-specific delivery packages that contain one or more order items from the same seller and share the same tracking information. This endpoint supports shipment management and order history screens where callers need to inspect shipment status, carrier data, and shipping progress without loading the full shipment detail payload.

Access is restricted by ownership and role. Customers may only see shipments belonging to their own orders, and sellers may only see shipments that contain their own order items. The service must validate pagination, filtering, and sorting inputs, return empty pages when nothing matches, and reject unauthorized access consistently with the platform’s authorization rules.

This endpoint does not modify shipment state. Completed shipments remain visible in browse results, but shipping creation, delivery confirmation, and other state changes are handled by separate operations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_shipments as a paginated collection.

Apply request-body filters for shipment status, seller scope, customer order scope, carrier name, tracking number, and date range if the corresponding fields are present in the request DTO. When the caller is a seller, constrain results to shipments containing the seller’s own order items. When the caller is a customer, constrain results to shipments related to the customer’s own orders. If the caller is an administrator, allow platform-wide access only if the surrounding authorization layer permits it.

Return summary rows only, sorted according to the requested sort mode and defaulting to newest first when unspecified. Do not fetch or embed the full nested shipment item graph unless needed for authorization checks. Validate pagination bounds, reject unsupported filters or sort keys, and return a standard empty page when no records match. If a shipment is inaccessible, treat it according to the platform’s existing not-found or forbidden conventions rather than leaking cross-account data.

responseBody.description: Paginated shipment summary records for browsing shipment history and tracking status.

requestBody.description: Shipment search criteria including pagination, filters, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Create a seller-specific shipment for one set of eligible order items.

This endpoint lets a seller group one or more of their order items into a single shipment and register shared tracking information for that package. All included items must belong to the same seller and must still require shipping; items from different sellers cannot be mixed in one shipment.

After successful creation, the shipment is linked to the selected order items and those items are marked as shipped. The shipment becomes visible in order details so customers can track the package and later confirm delivery for the shipment as a whole.

Validation errors are returned when the selected items are not eligible for shipping, when items already belong to another active shipment, when the shipment would mix sellers, or when the target order items cannot be found. The server must also reject attempts to create a shipment for a completed or otherwise unavailable shipping set.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target order items, verify that every item exists, belongs to the authenticated seller, and is in a shippable state (paid/waiting for shipment). Enforce that all items belong to the same seller and that each item is not already assigned to another active shipment. Reject completed or otherwise unavailable shipment attempts.

Create the shipment and shipment-item association records in a single transaction. Persist the carrier name and tracking number from the request body, then update each included order item's status to shipped. Ensure the shipment inherits the common seller context from the selected items and that no cross-seller grouping is possible.

If any item validation fails, abort the transaction and return a domain-appropriate error. Do not partially create shipments. Return the full shipment entity with its included shipment items and tracking fields after commit.

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment, including its tracking information and included order items.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation payload containing the eligible order items to bundle together and the shared tracking information for the package.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single shipment with its tracking information and included order items.

This endpoint returns the shipment detail view for one seller-specific package, including the shared carrier and tracking data, the shipment status, and the order items assigned to that shipment. The response is intended for both customers viewing order history and sellers reviewing fulfillment progress.

The shipment groups only order items from the same seller, so the returned item list should reflect that seller boundary and preserve the order context needed to show which purchased lines travel together. If the shipment does not exist, or the caller is not allowed to view it, the service should return the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by shipment_id and return the full shipment record with its related shipment items and each associated order item needed for display.

Join shipment_items to order_items, and for customer-facing views also include the order context necessary to verify that the shipment belongs to the caller’s order history. If the implementation needs to show item grouping, load the linked order item snapshots or summary fields already persisted on the order item as available in the schema.

Validate that the shipment exists before any relationship traversal. If the shipment is missing, return 404. If the caller is a customer, ensure the shipment belongs to one of that customer’s orders. If the caller is a seller, ensure the shipment belongs to items from that seller’s fulfillment scope. If access cannot be confirmed, return 403 or 404 according to the platform’s access-control convention.

Do not mutate shipment state in this operation. This endpoint is read-only and must not change delivery status, tracking fields, or item statuses. Preserve the shipment’s current state exactly as stored, including completed shipments that are no longer available for shipping actions.

responseBody.description: The full shipment record, including shared tracking information and the order items included in the shipment.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier (global scope).
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Updates the tracking details for a shipment.

A shipment represents one seller's delivery package for one or more order items, and all items in the package must belong to the same seller. This operation is intended for seller fulfillment workflows where the shipping carrier or tracking number needs to be corrected or revised after the shipment has been created.

The system must reject updates for shipments that are no longer available for shipping actions, including completed shipments. It must also preserve the seller grouping rule so that shipment contents remain internally consistent and cannot be changed to include items from another seller through this endpoint.

If the shipment does not exist, the request must fail with a not-found error. If the shipment is immutable because it has already been completed, the request must fail with a conflict or unavailable-state error. Validation errors should report invalid tracking information or any attempt to violate shipment consistency rules.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by shipment_id and lock it for update. Verify the shipment exists and belongs to the current seller or an administrator with shipment intervention authority. Reject the request if the shipment is completed or otherwise marked unavailable for shipping actions.

Update only mutable shipment fields such as carrier name and tracking number, and do not allow the request to move shipment items across sellers or to introduce items that do not belong to the shipment's seller. If the implementation permits shipment item adjustment in this endpoint, revalidate that every included order item belongs to the same seller and that none of the items are already assigned to another active shipment.

Persist changes in a transaction. Keep the existing shipment-item associations intact unless the schema explicitly supports controlled reassignment. Return the updated shipment together with its item set and tracking details. Surface validation failures for malformed tracking data, missing shipment, unauthorized access, or attempts to edit completed shipments.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment with its tracking information and associated order items.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier (UUID).
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: Shipment fields to update, such as carrier information and tracking number.

operations.description:
Delete a shipment record.

This operation removes a seller-specific shipment from active use. A shipment belongs to one seller and one order, and it groups order items that travel together with shared carrier and tracking information.

The shipment is identified by its UUID path parameter. The implementation must verify that the caller is allowed to manage the shipment, then mark the shipment as deleted in a way that keeps historical fulfillment data available for authorized views and dispute handling. Shipment-item assignments linked to the shipment are removed by the database relationship behavior, so the shipment no longer appears in active shipment lists or order views after deletion.

If the shipment does not exist, return a not-found error. If the caller is not authorized to delete the shipment, return an authorization error. The operation must not partially modify tracking fields or shipment-item membership when deletion fails.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Load mall_platform_shipments by UUID and verify it exists before writing. Confirm the caller has permission to manage the shipment in the owning seller or administrator scope. operations.description:
Update the order items assigned to a shipment.

This endpoint lets a seller revise which eligible order items are grouped into an existing shipment. A shipment may contain one or more order items, but all items must belong to the same seller, and items from different sellers cannot be combined into one shipment.

The update is validated as an all-or-nothing change. If any requested item is already assigned to another active shipment, is not eligible for shipping, or belongs to a different seller, the entire request is rejected and no changes are applied. If the shipment has already been completed or is otherwise unavailable, the request fails without modifying any associations.

The response returns the updated shipment item list so clients can refresh the shipment details and keep the tracking view in sync with the persisted shipment composition.

Perform the association changes inside a transaction. Remove shipment-item links that are no longer requested and create links for newly requested items. Prevent updates when the shipment is already completed or unavailable.

Return the refreshed shipment item page after persistence so downstream clients can render the updated package composition immediately.

operations.description:
Attach eligible order items to an existing shipment.

This endpoint creates shipment-item assignments for a seller-specific shipment so one package can contain one or more order items from the same seller. The shipment must already belong to the authenticated seller, and every order item included in the request must belong to that shipment's order and to the same seller as the shipment.

The service must reject items that are already assigned to another active shipment, items that do not belong to the target shipment order, and items that are no longer eligible for shipping. On success, the system creates shipment-item rows and preserves the shipment's shared tracking information at the shipment header level.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target shipment by id and verify it exists, is not deleted, and belongs to the current seller. Validate that the request contains at least one order item id and deduplicate the list before processing. For each order item, confirm it exists, is not deleted, belongs to the same order as the shipment, belongs to the same seller as the shipment, and is in a shippable status. Also verify the order item does not already have an existing shipment-item assignment because each eligible order item may belong to only one shipment at a time.

Create the shipment-item rows in a transaction to avoid partial assignment. If any item fails validation, reject the entire request and do not create any rows. After insert, return the created shipment-item records. Do not modify shipment header tracking fields here; this endpoint is only for item assignment. Use cascade-safe foreign key checks and surface not-found, forbidden, conflict, and validation errors clearly.

operations.description:
Removes one order item from a shipment.

This operation deletes the junction record that links a shipment to an order item, so the shipment can be adjusted without deleting the shipment itself or the purchased order item.

The server must confirm that the shipment-item association belongs to the requested shipment, that the caller is allowed to modify the shipment, and that the shipment is still available for shipping actions. Completed shipments are unavailable for further shipping actions, so their shipment-item links cannot be removed. If the link does not exist, the request must fail with a not-found error. The deletion must be atomic to keep the shipment package and its item membership consistent.

Load the mall_platform_shipment_items row by shipmentItemId and verify that mall_platform_shipment_id equals shipmentId. If the row is missing or belongs to another shipment, return not-found.

Before deleting, check the parent shipment record in mall_platform_shipments. Reject the mutation when the shipment is completed or otherwise unavailable for shipping actions. Enforce authorization so only the owning seller or an administrator can remove items from the shipment, according to platform access rules.

Perform the delete on mall_platform_shipment_items only. Do not delete the shipment, the order item, or any order data. If business logic requires recalculating shipment completeness after removing the last item, do so inside the same transaction. Keep the operation idempotent only in the sense that a missing association should still return not-found rather than silently succeeding.

operations.description:
Submits a cancellation request for one paid order item that has not been shipped.

This operation applies to exactly one order item identified by the path parameter. The customer submits a cancellation reason, and the system creates a cancellation request record that the seller of that item can later approve or reject. The request is item-scoped, so other items in the same order are not affected.

The server must verify that the authenticated customer owns the order containing the target item, that the item is in paid status, and that the item has not been shipped. If any of those conditions fail, the request must be rejected without changing the order item, inventory, shipment data, or other related records. The cancellation itself is not applied here; only the request is created.

When the request is reviewed later, the system must preserve the request state change in a snapshot for dispute review and history reconstruction. All failures must be atomic so the existing purchase history remains unchanged.
operations.name: patchByOrderitemid
operations.specification:
Look up the target order item by orderItemId and confirm that it belongs to the authenticated customer. Enforce the item-level cancellation rule: the item must be paid and must not have been shipped. Reject requests for cancelled, refunded, delivered, or otherwise ineligible items.

Create a cancellation request row linked to that order item, storing the submitted reason and the initial review state defined by the domain model. Do not modify the order item status at submission time. Do not create inventory movement records, do not touch shipment records, and do not alter order totals until an approval decision is made.

Use a transaction to guarantee that validation and insertion succeed or fail together. If a duplicate or conflicting cancellation request already exists for the item, return a business error and leave all data unchanged. Return the created request entity so the client can display the pending review state immediately.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request for the specified order item, including its review state and submitted reason.

Returns the immutable snapshot history for a specific cancellation request under a specific order item.

This endpoint is used to inspect how a cancellation request changed over time, including the before and after values recorded when the seller responded or the request content was updated. Snapshots are preserved for dispute resolution and historical reconstruction, so this operation only reads existing records and never creates, updates, or deletes them.

The cancellation request must belong to the specified order item. Results are returned in paginated form and should be sorted by newest snapshot first by default. Consumers may filter by time range or other searchable snapshot attributes supported by the request DTO. If the parent order item or cancellation request does not exist, or if the caller is not allowed to view the history, the service should return the standard not-found or forbidden error response used elsewhere in the platform.

Join or constrain by the parent cancellation request to ensure the nested route is consistent and prevent cross-item access. Treat snapshots as immutable records: do not expose any write path through this endpoint. Use the request body for pagination, keyword/search, and sorting controls consistent with list browsing expectations. Default ordering should be newest snapshot first, with stable secondary ordering by primary key if needed.

Authorization should allow the cancellation request owner, the relevant seller, and administrators to view the history, subject to the existing platform access rules. If the cancellation request or order item cannot be found in the nested scope, return not found. If the caller lacks access, return forbidden. If no snapshots exist yet, return an empty page rather than an error. Do not attempt to synthesize snapshot content; return only stored snapshot rows and their summary fields.

operations.description:
Search refund requests for a specific order item.

This endpoint returns the refund requests that belong to the referenced order item. It is intended for item-level refund review, allowing the caller to inspect the request reason and the current request state for that single purchased item.

Refund requests are scoped to one order item only, so the result never includes requests from other items. Access is limited to the customer who owns the order item, the seller responsible for the item, and administrators. If the parent order item does not exist or is not available to the caller, the request is rejected without exposing unrelated refund data.

When a refund request changes status, the system preserves snapshot history for dispute review and audit purposes. This endpoint lists the current refund request records; snapshots are stored separately and are not returned unless explicitly modeled by the summary DTO.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the parent order item by order_item identifier first so the collection is always scoped to one item and authorization can be checked against that exact purchase context. Query mall_platform_refund_requests filtered by the order item foreign key, then apply pagination, sorting, and any supported search filters from the request body.

Use a stable newest-first default sort with a deterministic secondary sort key for repeatable pages. Do not load refund requests for other order items. Do not synthesize an active request if none exists. If the parent item is deleted or otherwise unavailable, follow the platform’s historical-data and access rules, and return the appropriate business error when the caller is not allowed to view the item’s refund data.

The request body should support only criteria that correspond to actual refund request fields and common list controls such as page, page size, ordering, and state-based filtering. Keep the response shape as a paginated summary list suitable for management and customer UI screens.

responseBody.description: Paginated refund request summaries for the specified order item.

parameters.description: The identifier of the order item whose refund requests are being searched.

This endpoint returns the review feed shown on the product detail page. Results are restricted to the product identified in the path, ordered by newest first, and paginated so the client can render a stable review section even when the product has many reviews.

The returned reviews must follow the platform's public review rules. Reviews written by customers whose accounts were later removed must still be shown according to the deleted-user display rule, and deleted reviews must not be included in the active display set or the rating summary. If the product does not exist, the request must fail with a not-found error. If there are no reviews, the endpoint should return an empty page.

Preserve the display rule for removed customer accounts so historical feedback remains visible, but do not include deleted reviews in the active list or count. Do not mutate review records or snapshot rows. Return an empty page when the product has no reviews. operations.description:
Create a new product review for a delivered purchase.

This operation lets a customer submit feedback for a product they have already received. The review belongs to the customer who owns the purchased order item, and it becomes part of the product’s public review feed on the product detail page.

A review can be created only when the related order item has reached delivered status, and only one review may exist for the same product within the same order. The system must reject duplicate submissions for the same purchase context and any attempt to review an item that has not been delivered.

When the review is created, the platform records it as active review content and preserves historical integrity for later edits or deletions through snapshots. Deleted-user display handling is retained by the review model so the review can remain visible even if the original customer account is later removed.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated customer owns a delivered order item for the reviewed product before inserting the review.
Check that the same customer does not already have a review for the same product in the same order; reject duplicates with a conflict-style error.
Persist the review row in mall_platform_reviews using the actual schema fields, including rating and optional text content, and link it to the customer/order-item/product context required by the schema.
After insertion, create the corresponding immutable review snapshot record so later edits or deletions can be preserved for audit and dispute resolution.
Do not allow creation when the order item is not delivered, when the customer is not the purchaser, or when business rules indicate the review context is invalid.
Return a validation error for missing required rating or out-of-range values, and return a not-found or forbidden-style error when the purchase context does not belong to the caller.

responseBody.description: The newly created review, including its stored rating, optional text content, and identifiers needed for subsequent edit or delete actions.

requestBody.description: Review content for a delivered purchase, including the required rating and optional written feedback.

operations.description:
Update an existing customer review and preserve the prior version in snapshot history.

This operation allows the original reviewer to change the star rating and optional text content for a review that is shown on the product detail page. Reviews are part of the product’s public feedback history, so the service must record the previous state before saving the new content.

Only the customer who created the review may update it. The review must still be an active review linked to a valid purchase context, and the service must reject attempts to edit a missing review, another customer’s review, or a review that is no longer active. The edit must be saved together with an immutable snapshot so the previous rating and text remain available for audit and dispute review.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Fetch the review by reviewId and verify that it exists, is active, and belongs to the authenticated customer. Enforce the business rule that only the review owner may edit it. If authorization fails, return a not-found or forbidden response according to the platform’s access-control convention.

Validate the incoming rating and text content using the same constraints as review creation. Do not permit changes to ownership, product linkage, order linkage, timestamps, or any system-managed fields. Before persisting the new values, insert a review snapshot containing the previous persisted rating and text content. Perform the snapshot insert and review update in one transaction so the preserved history cannot diverge from the active record.

Return the updated review after the transaction commits. If the review does not exist, return not found. If validation fails, return the standard validation error response.

responseBody.description: The updated review after the edit has been saved and the previous state has been preserved in snapshot history.

requestBody.description: Editable review content consisting of the star rating and optional written text.

operations.description:
Delete one of the authenticated customer’s own reviews while preserving its history.

This operation removes the review from active customer feedback so it no longer appears in normal product detail displays or rating calculations. The platform must preserve prior review state through snapshots for audit, dispute resolution, and historical reconstruction, including cases where the customer account is later deleted and the review is shown as written by a deleted user.

The service must enforce ownership strictly. If the authenticated customer does not own the target review, the request must be rejected. If the review does not exist, the service must return a not-found error. If the review has already been deleted, the operation should keep the preserved history stable and avoid breaking the deleted-user presentation model.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the review by reviewId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject the request with forbidden when the ownership check fails, and with not found when the review does not exist.

Before changing the active-state marker, create a review snapshot that captures the current review content, rating, ownership reference, and timestamps needed for historical reconstruction. Then mark the review as deleted in the current review record so it is excluded from active review queries and average-rating calculations. Do not delete snapshot rows or otherwise mutate preserved review history.

Ensure the change is executed inside a transaction so snapshot creation and state mutation remain consistent. After deletion, refresh any cached or denormalized product rating aggregates so the deleted review no longer contributes to average rating or review counts used on product detail pages and listing surfaces.

If the implementation already treats repeated deletions as idempotent, return the current state without creating duplicate history. Otherwise, preserve the first deletion snapshot as the authoritative historical record.

This endpoint returns the preserved history of review edits and deletion-related state changes for the specified review. It is intended for the review owner and administrators to compare previous values, inspect when changes occurred, and support dispute resolution or historical review.

The response is paginated because a review may accumulate multiple snapshots over time. Results should be ordered according to the requested sorting rules, with the most recent snapshots typically shown first. If the review does not exist or the caller is not allowed to view its history, the request must be rejected with the appropriate authorization or not-found error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Load the review by reviewId and verify the caller can access its snapshot history. Access is allowed to the review owner and administrators only. Query the mall_platform_review_snapshots table for rows related to the review, ordered by the requested sort fields, with pagination applied. If the underlying review has been deleted, continue to return preserved snapshots when the business rules require retained history. Do not allow any mutation of snapshot rows. If the reviewId is invalid or no matching review exists, return not-found. If the caller lacks permission, return forbidden. Include search/filter support only for snapshot-related browsing fields if those are defined in the request DTO; do not infer unsupported filters.

responseBody.description: Paginated review snapshot summaries for the specified review, including immutable history rows that can be used to inspect prior values and change timing.

Retrieve one immutable snapshot for a specific review.

This endpoint returns a preserved point-in-time record of a review so authorized consumers can inspect historical rating, text content, and change metadata for dispute resolution or audit review. Snapshots remain available even after the live review is edited or deleted.

Access is restricted to the review owner, administrators, and any other actors allowed by the platform's visibility rules. If the review does not exist, the snapshot does not exist, or the snapshot does not belong to the specified review, the service must return not found. operations.name: at

Return the full snapshot entity with preserved review state and snapshot metadata, including the change timestamp and before/after values required for historical inspection.

operations.description:
Browse immutable product snapshots with pagination and filtering.

This endpoint returns preserved product history records for review, audit, and dispute resolution. Each snapshot represents the state of a product at a point in time, including the product fields that were captured when a change succeeded. Because snapshots are immutable, this operation is read-only and does not modify any product, variant, or image data.

Access is intended for administrators and other authorized viewers who need to inspect historical product state, including the preserved product presentation and variant context captured in the snapshot. If the requested page exceeds the available history, an empty page is returned. If filters do not match any records, the response contains no items rather than an error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_product_snapshots as the root data set and apply pagination, sorting, and snapshot-history filters from the request body. Return a paginated list of snapshot summaries ordered by the requested sort, defaulting to the most recently created snapshot records first.

Support filtering by product identity and any snapshot-history criteria defined in the request DTO. If the implementation needs to expose related snapshot details, join or hydrate the preserved product snapshot relations only for summary-safe fields; do not attempt to reconstruct mutable current product state. Keep the operation read-only and never create, update, or delete snapshot rows because snapshot records are immutable by business rule.

When no records match, return an empty page. When the requested page is beyond the available data, still return a valid page object with zero items. Do not infer deleted-current-product state as a failure, because historical snapshot records remain available even after the live product changes or is removed.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of immutable product snapshot summaries for historical browsing and dispute review.

requestBody.description: Pagination, sorting, and snapshot-history filters for browsing immutable product snapshot records.
