operations.description:
Retrieve a single immutable product snapshot by its identifier.

This endpoint returns the preserved historical state of a product at the moment the snapshot was created, including the product data and its related snapshot content for images and variants. It is intended for audit review, historical inspection, and dispute resolution, and it never mutates the stored snapshot.

Access should be limited to the owning seller of the original product and administrators. If the snapshot does not exist, the service should return a not-found response. Because snapshots are immutable records, the response must reflect exactly what was stored when the snapshot was created and must not recalculate current product data.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the product snapshot row by productSnapshotId and return the full immutable snapshot record.
Include the preserved nested snapshot data needed to reconstruct the product's historical presentation, especially the image history and variant-state history captured with the snapshot.

Authorize access for the owning seller of the original product and administrators only. If the identifier is invalid or no snapshot exists, return not found. If the caller is not permitted to view the snapshot, return forbidden.

Do not read from the live products or product_variants tables to compose historical state. The snapshot itself is the source of truth, and no mutation is allowed.

Lists preserved order item snapshots with filtering and pagination.

This endpoint returns immutable historical records captured for order item changes so authorized users can review purchase-state history during disputes, refunds, cancellations, and administrative review. Each snapshot belongs to one order item and preserves the item status, product details, seller shop identity, quantity, and line totals at the time the snapshot was recorded.

Filtering and sorting are intended for browsing historical records, not for modifying them. The response is paginated because snapshot history can grow over time, and consumers may need to narrow results by order item, snapshot time, or reason. The records are immutable and cannot be created, edited, or deleted through this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_order_item_snapshots as immutable history records.
Apply filters from the request body to support order item scope, snapshot time ranges, snapshot reason text search, and ordering by created timestamp or snapshot timestamp when available in the request contract.
Join to mall_platform_order_items only as needed for scope validation or display enrichment, but keep the response as summary rows to avoid overfetching full snapshot payloads.
Return paginated results ordered by most recent snapshots first by default.

operations.description:
Submit a new administrator approval request for governance review.

This endpoint lets an authenticated customer or seller formally request administrator access by providing a reason for the request. The created record starts in a pending review state and becomes part of the platform’s immutable governance history once it is submitted.

The caller must be an eligible non-admin account. If the account state is unavailable for business operations, or if the caller is otherwise not allowed to request administrator access, the request must be rejected. The submitted reason is required because the review workflow must preserve the applicant’s justification alongside the final decision.

The response returns the created approval request so the client can display the pending status immediately after submission.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new row in mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests for the authenticated customer or seller.
Validate that the caller is an eligible non-admin account allowed to request administrator access.
Persist the submitted reason and initialize the request in the pending state required by the governance workflow.
Return the newly created request after insert.
Reject the operation when the caller is not eligible, when the reason is missing or invalid, or when the account state is unavailable for business operations.
Do not create a snapshot at submission time unless the persistence layer explicitly requires it; snapshots are needed when the request is reviewed and its status changes.

responseBody.description: The administrator approval request that was created successfully and is now pending review.

requestBody.description: Submission payload containing the applicant's reason for requesting administrator access.

operations.description:
Finalize an administrator approval request.

This endpoint lets a super administrator approve or reject an administrator access request submitted by a customer or seller. The request keeps the applicant’s reason and the final review outcome so the platform can preserve a traceable governance history.

Only pending requests may be processed. Once a request has been approved or rejected, it must not be processed again. If the request is approved, the applicant is granted regular administrator access. If it is rejected, the request remains a rejected governance record with the decision preserved for later review.

If the request does not exist, is already completed, or the caller lacks super administrator privileges, the service must reject the operation with the appropriate authorization or validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Fetch the administrator approval request by approvalRequestId and enforce row-level locking while applying the review decision. Verify that the caller has super administrator privileges before any state change. Reject requests that are missing or not currently pending to satisfy the rule that completed requests cannot be processed again.

Apply the update from the request body as a governance decision payload. Persist the final status as approved or rejected, and store any reviewer reason or notes required by the business workflow. Do not overwrite the original applicant reason; it must remain attached to the record for oversight review.

When the request is approved, activate or grant the corresponding regular administrator account according to the platform's administrator onboarding flow. When rejected, keep the record as a permanent rejected governance item. Return the updated request after commit so the client can display the final decision immediately.

responseBody.description: The administrator approval request after the review decision has been saved, including the final status and reviewer outcome details.

This operation is intended for super administrators who need to inspect pending, approved, and rejected administrator requests. It supports filtering, sorting, and pagination so review queues can be managed efficiently without exposing the data to general browsing.

Each result reflects the applicant reason, current review status, and review outcome stored in the administrator approval request record. The response should only include records the caller is authorized to view, and empty result sets should be returned as an empty page rather than as an error.

Invalid search criteria, unsupported filters, or insufficient privileges must be rejected with an appropriate error response.

Query mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests with pagination, filtering, and sorting support. The query should expose review-oriented fields such as status and other request attributes defined by the request DTO, but must not invent columns outside the schema.

Use a stable ordering strategy suitable for paginated review queues. Return a paginated summary projection optimized for list display, not the full entity. This is a read-only operation and must not modify request status, review outcome, or timestamps.

Enforce administrator authorization before querying. Validate pagination inputs, reject unsupported sort keys or filters, and return an empty page when no records match. If the caller lacks permission, deny access before executing the database query.

This endpoint returns the full administrator approval request record, including the applicant administrator reference, the submitted reason, the current review status, and any reviewer decision details. It is used by super administrators to inspect pending or finalized administrator access requests and to preserve a traceable approval history.

The response may include a rejected request’s rejection reason and review timestamp, or an approved request’s decision metadata. If the record cannot be found or the caller is not allowed to view governance records, the service should return the appropriate not-found or authorization error.

Validate that approvalRequestId is a UUID. If no row exists, return not found. If the caller lacks permission to access administrator governance data, return forbidden. Do not create, update, or delete any database state in this operation.

Preserve the persisted status and review metadata exactly as stored. If the implementation hides rows with deleted_at for normal access, apply that visibility rule consistently here while still supporting audit-oriented behavior when required by the platform rules.

operations.description:
Creates a new administrator approval request for an authenticated customer or seller.

This operation submits the caller's request to gain administrator privileges. The caller must provide a reason that explains why elevated access is being requested, and the system stores the request in a pending state for later review by a super administrator.

The request becomes part of the platform's governance history. Approved requests grant regular administrator access, rejected requests do not grant access, and the stored record preserves the submitted reason and final review outcome for traceability. Validation errors are returned when the caller is not eligible to submit the request, when the reason is missing or invalid, or when an unresolved administrator request already exists for the same account.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new row in mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests for the authenticated account.
Validate that the caller is an eligible customer or seller account and that the account state permits submitting an administrator request. Require the reason field from the request body and initialize the new request with a pending review status.

Before inserting, check whether the same applicant already has an unresolved administrator approval request. If one exists, reject the request with a conflict or validation error to prevent duplicate submissions. Use a transaction so the duplicate check and insert are atomic under concurrent submissions.

Do not expose or accept review decision fields in the create payload. The review outcome belongs to the administrator review workflow, not the submission workflow. Return clear errors for missing reason, invalid caller type, suspended/banned/unavailable account state, and duplicate pending requests.

responseBody.description: The newly created administrator approval request, including its pending status and submitted reason.

requestBody.description: Submission payload for creating an administrator approval request. The payload must include the reason for requesting administrator privileges.

operations.description:
Update an administrator approval request with the stored review decision.

This endpoint records the final governance decision for a request submitted by a customer or seller who wants administrator access. The approval record keeps the applicant’s original reason together with the final status so the platform can preserve a traceable review history.

Only a super administrator should be allowed to use this operation. The service must prevent changes that would rewrite the original applicant context or bypass the pending-to-finalized workflow. If the request has already been resolved, the update should be rejected instead of silently overwriting the existing decision.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Fetch the administrator approval request by approvalRequestId and verify that it exists. Enforce super-administrator authorization before applying any change. Update only the review decision fields allowed by the business workflow, preserving the applicant reference and original submission reason.

Persist the status transition and decision atomically so the record never ends in a partially updated state. If the schema includes reviewer or decided-at fields, write them together with the decision in the same transaction. Return the updated record after persistence.

Reject the request with not found when the ID does not exist, forbidden when the caller lacks super-administrator access, and conflict or validation errors when the request is already finalized or the payload does not conform to the approval workflow.

operations.description:
Ends the current authenticated session for the signed-in account.

This operation applies only to the user’s active session, whether the user is a customer, seller, or administrator. It immediately stops the platform from treating the caller as signed in, while leaving the underlying account data unchanged.

The server must invalidate the current session record and ensure that authenticated features can no longer be accessed with the same session. If the session has already ended or is otherwise unavailable, the operation should still complete without affecting any other user’s session.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Invalidate the currently authenticated session for the caller and remove or deactivate the corresponding session record in the session store. Resolve the caller’s actor type from the authentication context and ensure only the current session is affected.

Do not modify customer, seller, or administrator profile data, credentials, approvals, carts, orders, or any other account records. If the session is already expired, missing, or otherwise unusable, return a successful logout result so the client can treat the session as ended. Ensure the operation cannot terminate another user’s session and cannot be used without an authenticated context.

operations.description:
Returns the current approval status of the authenticated seller account.

This endpoint exposes the seller registration state as one of the platform visibility values: pending, approved, or rejected. If the seller has been rejected, the response also includes the rejection reason so the seller can understand the decision and decide whether to submit a new registration request.

The operation is restricted to the caller’s own seller account and does not modify approval state, seller profile data, or any other account fields.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Authenticate the caller as a seller and load the seller account associated with the current session. Return the seller approval status directly from mall_platform_seller_accounts, including the rejection reason when the stored status is rejected.

Reject unauthenticated requests and any request that is not made by a valid seller principal. Do not expose unrelated seller fields, do not modify any records, and do not create snapshots because this endpoint is read-only. If the authenticated seller account cannot be resolved, return the appropriate authorization or not-found error.

responseBody.description: The authenticated seller account’s current approval status and optional rejection reason.

operations.description:
Terminates the caller's current authenticated session.

This endpoint is used for logout flows. It invalidates the active session associated with the current request so the credentials can no longer be used for subsequent authenticated requests.

The operation is idempotent. If the session is already expired, revoked, or missing, the request should still complete successfully. No path parameter or request body is required, and authentication is resolved from the request context before the session is removed.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Resolve the current authenticated session from the request context and revoke it in the session store for the corresponding actor type. Remove any persistent session record and invalidate any associated refresh credential if one exists. If the session is already gone or expired, return success to preserve idempotent logout semantics. Do not accept a session identifier in the URL or body, and do not expose session metadata in the response.

operations.description:
Returns the current storefront identity for the authenticated seller account.

The storefront identity is the customer-visible representation of a seller and is defined by the shop name, shop description, and logo image stored in the seller profile. This operation is used by storefront pages and customer-facing product views to display the merchant's brand consistently.

The response reflects the seller profile as it exists now. Historical storefront versions are preserved separately through seller profile snapshots and are not modified by this request. If the caller is not authenticated as a seller, or if the seller profile cannot be resolved, the request must fail with the appropriate authorization or not-found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Resolve the seller profile for the current authenticated seller account and return only the storefront identity fields required for customer-facing display: shop name, shop description, and logo image reference. Do not include credentials, approval metadata, or other internal seller account fields. No write action occurs. If the caller is unauthorized, return an authorization error. If the seller profile does not exist, return a not-found error.

responseBody.description: The current customer-visible storefront identity for the authenticated seller account, including the shop name, shop description, and logo image.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated seller’s storefront identity.

This operation changes the seller profile values that define the public shop identity shown to customers: shop name, shop description, and logo image. It is restricted to the currently authenticated seller and does not change account credentials or approval status.

A successful edit must create a seller profile snapshot that preserves the previous storefront identity alongside the updated values. If validation, authorization, or persistence fails, the seller profile must remain unchanged and no snapshot may be recorded.

The updated storefront identity is used in customer-facing pages such as product listings, product detail pages, and historical order records. Clients should expect authorization errors when the caller is not the owner of the seller profile.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated seller from the security context and load that seller’s profile. Validate the incoming storefront identity fields against seller profile rules before making any database change.

Apply the update inside a single transaction. After the profile is updated successfully, create a seller profile snapshot capturing the prior and current storefront identity values so the edit history is preserved. If any validation, authorization, or persistence step fails, roll back the transaction and do not create a snapshot.

Return the updated seller profile after commit. Reject requests when the caller is not a seller, when the seller profile does not exist, or when the caller is not allowed to edit its own storefront identity.

responseBody.description: The updated seller profile representing the seller’s current storefront identity after a successful edit.

requestBody.description: The storefront identity fields to update for the authenticated seller’s own profile.

operations.description:
Returns the current storefront identity for one seller account.

This operation exposes the public shop presentation for the specified seller, including the shop name, shop description, and logo image. The storefront identity is the live seller profile shown on customer-facing pages, and it is also the identity preserved in historical purchase records.

The seller is identified by the path parameter. If the seller account does not exist, the request fails with a not found error. The operation is read-only and does not change the seller profile or create any snapshot.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the seller profile associated with sellerId and return the public storefront identity fields from mall_platform_seller_profiles. Validate that the seller account exists and that a profile record is available; if the account is missing, return 404, and if the profile row is missing, treat it as a server-side data integrity error.

Return the storefront identity only. Do not include authentication fields, approval status, internal moderation data, or any fields not part of the customer-facing profile. This endpoint must not write data or create snapshots because it is purely a read operation.

responseBody.description: The current seller profile storefront identity, including shop name, description, and logo image reference.

parameters.description: The UUID of the seller account whose storefront identity should be returned.

operations.description:
List the immutable storefront identity snapshots for a seller profile.

This operation returns historical records of a seller's storefront identity, including the captured shop name, shop description, logo image URI, and creation timestamp for each snapshot. These records exist to preserve prior storefront states for audit and dispute review, and they reflect the exact values stored in `mall_platform_seller_profile_snapshots`.

Access is limited to the seller profile owner and administrators. The endpoint is read-only because snapshots are immutable and remain available even after the related seller profile is edited or removed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query `mall_platform_seller_profile_snapshots` as an immutable history dataset scoped to the target seller profile. Filter and paginate the result set according to the request body criteria, and sort by `created_at` descending unless the request explicitly requests another supported sort order. Return only the stored snapshot fields: `seller_profile_id`, `shop_name`, `shop_description`, `logo_image_uri`, and `created_at`.

Enforce access control so that only the seller profile owner or an administrator can read these snapshots. If the caller is unauthorized, return a forbidden error. If the requested scope cannot be resolved, return a not-found error according to platform conventions. Do not implement create, update, or delete behavior for snapshots because the underlying records are append-only and immutable.

This endpoint lets the seller owner and administrators inspect immutable seller profile snapshots that preserve prior storefront identity values. Each snapshot reflects a completed seller profile edit and records the historical shop name, shop description, and logo image reference used at that time.

The result is scoped to the seller account in the path. Clients can browse the snapshot timeline for audit and dispute resolution, but they cannot create, edit, or delete snapshot records through this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_seller_profile_snapshots for the seller identified by sellerId and return a paginated list of snapshot summaries ordered from newest to oldest. Enforce seller ownership or administrator access at the authorization layer.

This is a read-only history endpoint. Do not mutate any snapshot rows. If the seller does not exist, return not found. If the caller lacks permission, return forbidden. The request body should support the shared list/search pagination contract only; use the snapshot summary schema for the response so clients can render a timeline without loading the full entity details.

operations.description:
Confirms delivery for a shipment belonging to the authenticated customer.

Delivery confirmation is handled per shipment, not per order item. When this action succeeds, every order item included in the selected shipment changes to delivered status, while other shipments in the same order remain unchanged. The shipment must already belong to an order owned by the caller and must be in a confirmable state.

This endpoint is used from order history and shipment detail views. If the shipment is already completed, unavailable, or does not belong to the caller, the request must fail with a conflict, not-found, or authorization error as appropriate.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by ID and verify that it exists, is owned indirectly through an order belonging to the authenticated customer, and is eligible for delivery confirmation. Reject the request if the shipment has already been confirmed, is unavailable, or is not owned by the caller.

Perform the status change in a single transaction. Mark the shipment as confirmed/completed and update every included order item to delivered. Do not touch other shipments in the order and do not modify items outside the selected shipment. The operation must respect the rule that customer delivery confirmation applies to the whole shipment at once.

Return the refreshed shipment entity, including its included items and tracking information, so the UI can render the updated order detail state. Map repeated confirmation attempts to a conflict or unavailable-style error instead of creating duplicate records.

responseBody.description: The shipment after delivery confirmation, including the updated shipment status and its contained order items.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier to confirm delivery for.
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Force-cancel an order or selected order items as an administrator intervention.

This endpoint lets an administrator override the normal purchase flow for exceptional policy enforcement or dispute resolution. The cancellation is applied in the context of the target order so the platform can preserve the order record, item history, and any existing snapshots while updating the affected item states and restoring stock through inventory history.

The operation is item-level by business rule. If the intervention covers every item in the order, the order becomes fully cancelled; if only some items are cancelled, the remaining items continue through their own lifecycle. If the request fails validation, targets an ineligible item, or cannot be completed safely, no partial state changes may be committed.
operations.name: forceCancel
operations.specification:
Authorize the caller as an administrator before any data access. Load the target order by orderId and resolve the items affected by the force-cancel command.

Perform the intervention in a single database transaction. For each targeted order item, verify it belongs to the order and can be transitioned to cancelled according to the platform's order intervention rules. Do not delete the order, order items, or any historical snapshot data. Recompute the overall order state from the resulting item states after the cancellation completes. If every item is cancelled, mark the order as fully cancelled; otherwise keep the order in the appropriate mixed state derived from the remaining active items.

operations.description:
Force a refund outcome for an order under administrator oversight.

This action is used when a privileged administrator must intervene in an order for policy enforcement, dispute resolution, or other exceptional cases. The platform applies the refund outcome to the relevant order item or items, preserves the historical record, and restores stock through inventory history when the refund is completed.

The operation targets a specific order identified by `orderId`. It should only be allowed for administrators with order intervention authority. If the order does not exist, the requester is not authorized, or the order cannot be forced into a refund state because of its current item statuses or request history, the service should return an appropriate error response. When successful, the response returns the updated order view so consumers can confirm the forced refund result.
operations.name: create

Apply the refund outcome to the relevant item(s) according to the platform's intervention policy, using the same state transitions and side effects required for a normal refund outcome. If the intervention covers items that were previously shipped or delivered, ensure the service still records the administrative override and preserves order history.

Preserve all historical records and any existing snapshots associated with the order item or refund-related entities.

The operation must be transactional. If any part of the intervention fails, roll back the entire change set so the order, order items, inventory history, and snapshots remain consistent. operations.description:
Returns the seller's order items that are eligible to be added to a new shipment.

This operation is used during seller fulfillment so a merchant can choose one or more of their own order items that still need shipping. Eligible items are limited to the authenticated seller's own order items, and each item must not already belong to another shipment. Items from different sellers are never combined in the same shipment, so the returned list is scoped to a single seller's fulfillment work.

The response is intended for shipment creation screens and similar seller workflows. Consumers should expect only items that are still available for shipping, with shipment membership constraints already applied. If there are no eligible items, the page is returned empty rather than raising an error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Determine the authenticated seller from the request context, then query mall_platform_order_items joined with mall_platform_shipments and mall_platform_shipment_items to find order items that are still eligible for shipment creation.

Only return order items that belong to the seller, are in a shippable state, and do not already have a shipment_item assignment. Exclude items that are already assigned to any shipment, because each eligible order item may belong to only one shipment at a time. Respect the seller grouping rule so items from other sellers are never included.

Support pagination and default sorting by newest eligible item first, using created_at descending unless the broader interface standard requires a different default. Return an empty page when no eligible items exist. Do not mutate any records in this operation.

operations.description:
Returns the paginated list of pending shipments that are still available for shipping-related processing.

This endpoint is meant for operational queue views where sellers or authorized administrators inspect shipments that have not yet reached a completed state. Completed shipments must not appear in this result set, because completed shipment records are unavailable for further shipping actions.

Each shipment represents one seller's package and may contain one or more order items from that seller. The response therefore exposes shipment-level summaries rather than item-level records, keeping seller grouping intact and preventing items from different sellers from being combined.

If the caller is not allowed to inspect shipment queues, the request must be rejected. Invalid pagination, search, or sorting criteria should return a validation error. When there are no pending shipments, the endpoint should return an empty page rather than an error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shipment records that are still pending and exclude any shipment that has already been completed. Apply any search, pagination, and sorting criteria provided in the request body before returning results.

Use the shipment lifecycle state to identify actionable shipments. Do not include completed shipments, and do not create or modify shipment records in this operation. Return only summary data suitable for queue browsing.

Enforce authorization before querying. If the current actor cannot inspect shipment queues, return a forbidden response. If no matching shipments are found, return an empty page. If related data is inconsistent, fail the request with a server error rather than returning partial data.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of pending shipment summaries for queue browsing and shipping workflows.

operations.description:
Returns the tracking details for a single shipment.

A shipment is the package delivery unit for one seller, so its carrier name, tracking number, optional tracking URL, and delivery timestamps apply to every order item included in that shipment. This endpoint is used to present shipment-level tracking information from the order detail view and other shipment lookup screens.

The response maps directly to the shipment record stored in `mall_platform_shipments`, including the shipment status and the shipped and delivered timestamps when available. Because tracking is shared at the shipment level, the endpoint does not expose per-item tracking differences.

If the shipment does not exist, the request must fail with a not-found error. If the caller is not allowed to view the shipment, the service must reject the request according to platform authorization rules. Soft-deleted shipments should not be returned if the implementation excludes records with a populated `deleted_at` value.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch one shipment by its UUID from mall_platform_shipments and return its tracking-related fields.
Include carrier_name, tracking_number, tracking_url, status, shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at, and updated_at in the response mapping if supported by the response DTO.
Enforce access control so the owning customer, the owning seller, or an administrator can access the record according to the platform's authorization rules.
Reject missing shipments with not found. Do not accept a request body. Do not query order-item tracking separately because tracking is defined only at the shipment level and shared by all items in the shipment.

operations.description:
Approves a cancellation request for the specified order item.

This endpoint lets the seller responsible for the order item accept a customer's cancellation request after verifying that the request belongs to the given order item and is still pending. The approval decision is recorded as part of the request history so the platform can preserve the full decision trail for dispute review.

When approval succeeds, the system updates the cancellation request status, records an immutable snapshot of the request state, cancels the order item if it has not already reached a final outcome, and restores inventory for the affected quantity through a new inventory record. Any downstream refund handling required by the cancellation workflow is also triggered as part of the same transaction.

If the request does not belong to the specified order item, is not pending, or the order item is no longer eligible for cancellation, the operation must fail without changing the stored request. Authorization must ensure only the seller who owns the order item, or an explicitly permitted administrator role, can execute the approval.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the cancellation request by cancellationRequestId and verify it belongs to orderItemId before making any state changes. Reject the request with a not-found, forbidden, or conflict error if the association does not match, if the request is not pending, or if the order item is already in a final state that prevents cancellation.

Perform the approval in a single transaction. Insert cancellation-request snapshot records according to the snapshot model so the pre-decision and post-decision state can be reconstructed later. Update the cancellation request with the approved outcome and any reviewer metadata required by the schema. If the order item has not yet reached a final outcome, change its status to cancelled and create an inventory record that restores the cancelled quantity for the related product variant. Trigger any refund-processing flow required by the cancellation approval policy.

If concurrent processing has already finalized the order item, keep the final item outcome unchanged while still storing the seller response in the request history. Return the updated cancellation request after the transaction commits. Do not expose unrelated order-item fields in the response body.

responseBody.description: The cancellation request after the seller's approval has been recorded.

parameters.description: The identifier of the order item that owns the cancellation request.
parameters.name: orderItemId

parameters.description: The identifier of the cancellation request to approve within the specified order item scope.
parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

operations.description:
Reject a cancellation request for a specific order item.

This operation is used by the seller who owns the order item, and by an administrator when platform permissions allow intervention, to record a rejection decision on a pending cancellation request. The request is always scoped to one order item, so the system must verify that the cancellation request belongs to the specified order item before applying any change.

When the rejection is accepted, the system updates the cancellation request status, stores the reviewer decision as part of the request history, and creates an immutable snapshot of the request state for dispute review. If the request is already closed or otherwise finalized, the system must preserve the existing state and reject the attempt to overwrite it.

Typical failures include a missing or mismatched order item relationship, unauthorized access, an invalid request state, or a request that no longer belongs to the specified item.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Load the order item and cancellation request with a scoped query that confirms the request belongs to the specified item. Enforce ownership so only the seller of the item or an authorized administrator can perform the rejection.

Reject the operation if the cancellation request is not in a pending review state or if it has already reached a final outcome. On success, update the request status to rejected, persist the reviewer decision details, and insert a cancellation-request snapshot capturing the prior state and the newly rejected state. Do not change the order item status, payment state, or inventory on rejection.

Execute the status update and snapshot insert in a single transaction. If the relationship check fails, return a not found or conflict-style error rather than partially updating the record. Return the updated cancellation request entity after commit.

operations.description:
Returns the public review list for a specific product.

This endpoint provides the review feed displayed on the product detail page. Reviews are ordered with the newest entries first by default so customers can see the latest buyer feedback before older comments.

The list is scoped to the product identified by `productId`, and only reviews belonging to that product are returned. Deleted reviews remain preserved in history, but they must not contribute to active rating display or the visible review list used for customer browsing. The total count and pagination results should align with the active review set used for product detail presentation.

If the product does not exist, the service must return a not-found error. If pagination parameters are invalid, the service must reject the request with a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target product by productId first and confirm it exists. Query mall_platform_reviews for the matching product, excluding deleted reviews from the visible result set if the schema exposes a deletion state, and order results by created_at descending to match newest-first display. Apply pagination from the request body, and support optional search/sort fields if they are defined in the request DTO, but keep newest-first as the default order.

The response must be a paginated summary collection suitable for the product detail page. Each row should expose the review rating, text content, author display context if available through the review schema, and review timestamps only if they exist in the schema. Do not invent fields that are not present. If the product has no active reviews, return an empty page rather than an error.

When calculating any count metadata for the page, use the same active review filter so the count matches what customers see. Reject requests for inaccessible products according to platform authorization rules. Return 404 when the product identifier does not resolve, and return 400 for invalid pagination or sort inputs.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of public review summaries for the specified product.

parameters.description: The product identifier that scopes the review list.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Search, sorting, and pagination criteria for the product review list.

operations.description:
Resolve the ownership identity and display status for a single review.

This endpoint is used when the platform needs to determine how a review should be presented to customers, sellers, or administrators. A review always remains owned by the customer who wrote it, and if that customer account has been deleted, the review must continue to be shown as written by a deleted user while preserving the ownership relationship for dispute resolution and history viewing.

The operation does not modify review data or create snapshots. If the review does not exist, the server must return not found. If the caller is not allowed to inspect review ownership information, the request must be rejected according to the platform’s access rules.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the review row by reviewId and derive ownership presentation from the stored customer ownership reference plus the current existence of the customer account. If the customer account is missing or deleted, return a deleted-user presentation state while preserving the ownership relationship in the response.

This endpoint is read-only and must not update review records, customer records, or snapshots. Return 404 when the review cannot be found. Enforce authorization before returning the result so only permitted parties can view ownership details, consistent with review visibility, owner access, and administrative oversight rules.

responseBody.description: Ownership and display-state information for the requested review, including whether it should be shown under an active customer account or as deleted-user content.

operations.description:
Returns the review summary for a product.

This endpoint supports product detail pages by providing the aggregate review information needed to display product reputation, including the average rating and total review count, without loading the full list of reviews.

Only active reviews should be counted in the summary. If the product has no active reviews, the endpoint should still return a valid summary with zero counts or equivalent empty-state values defined by the response schema. If the product does not exist, the service must return a not-found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the product by product_id and verify that it exists before computing any aggregate values.

Query mall_platform_reviews for the requested product and include only reviews that are still active. Exclude deleted reviews from both the average rating calculation and the review count so the returned data matches the public product detail page behavior.

Return a single summary object only; do not include the full review list. This operation must not mutate products, reviews, or snapshot records. If no active reviews exist, return a valid empty summary instead of an error. If the product is missing, return a not-found response.

operations.description:
Returns the immutable history for a single review.

This endpoint exposes the preserved snapshot timeline for a review so the caller can inspect prior ratings, text content, and deletion-preservation state. It is intended for dispute resolution, owner self-service, and administrative review, while keeping the active review entity separate from its historical versions.

The service must return the full set of snapshots associated with the review in chronological order, including the values captured before and after each edit or deletion event when available. If the review does not exist, return not found. If the caller is neither the review owner nor an administrator, return forbidden. If the review exists but no snapshots have been created yet, return an empty history collection.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the target review by review_id and verify the caller is authorized to view its history. Authorization should allow the original review owner and administrators; other callers must be rejected.

Query mall_platform_review_snapshots for all rows linked to the review, ordered by snapshot timestamp or snapshot identifier ascending so the response reconstructs the full change timeline. Do not attempt to synthesize live review state; return only immutable history records. If the review is missing, return not found. If there are no snapshots, return an empty collection with a successful response.

Keep the response read-only and do not expose any write paths here. The endpoint must not alter review status, ownership, or deletion flags.

responseBody.description: Immutable review snapshot history for the requested review, including preserved prior versions and deletion-related history.

parameters.description: The review identifier whose preserved history is being requested.

operations.specification:

Apply any platform-wide paging and sorting conventions used by other browse endpoints. Do not mutate snapshot rows, and do not trigger snapshot creation as a side effect of reading. operations.description:
Approve a pending administrator approval request.

This operation is used by a super administrator to approve one existing administrator request that is still under review. When the approval succeeds, the request status is updated to approved, the review decision is recorded, and the requesting user gains regular administrator privileges according to the platform governance workflow.

Access is restricted to super administrators only. If a regular administrator or any other actor attempts to call this endpoint, the request must be rejected and the underlying approval request must remain unchanged. If the target request is not pending, the service should reject the action because the review has already been resolved.

The approval request record is part of the administrator governance domain and should preserve reviewer decision details for audit and dispute review. Any response should reflect the latest persisted state of the request after approval.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the administrator approval request by administratorApprovalRequestId and verify it exists.
Verify the authenticated caller has super administrator privileges; reject all non-super administrators with a forbidden error.
Allow approval only when the request is currently pending; if it is already approved or rejected, return a conflict or validation error and do not modify the record.
On success, update the request status to approved and persist the reviewer decision metadata and review timestamp fields defined by the administrator approval request schema.
If the domain requires creating a corresponding administrator account transition, perform it in the same transaction so the request status and privilege change remain consistent.
Return the fully updated administrator approval request entity after the transaction commits.

responseBody.description: The approved administrator approval request with its updated status and decision metadata.

parameters.description: The administrator approval request identifier to approve (UUID, scoped to a single request).
parameters.name: administratorApprovalRequestId

operations.description:
Reject an administrator approval request that is still pending.

This operation is used by super administrators to complete the review of an administrator approval request. A rejected request remains recorded with its final outcome so that the original applicant does not gain administrator privileges and the review cannot be processed again.

Only super administrators are allowed to perform this action. If the request is already approved or rejected, the system must reject the operation and leave the stored request unchanged. The response includes the updated approval request so clients can show the final review state and rejection result.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Load the administrator approval request by administratorApprovalRequestId and verify it exists.
Verify the authenticated user is a super administrator; regular administrators and other roles must receive a forbidden response.
Verify the request is still pending before applying the rejection. If the request is already finalized, return a conflict-style business error and preserve the stored state.
Within a transaction, update the approval request status to rejected and persist the review outcome metadata required by the schema, including the reviewer identity and decision timestamp if those fields exist in the table definition.
Do not modify the applicant's administrator role when rejecting. The rejection only closes the approval request workflow.
Return the updated approval request entity after reload so the caller sees the final rejected state. If the request is missing, return not found. If authorization fails, return forbidden. If the request is not pending, return an error indicating the decision cannot be applied again.

responseBody.description: The administrator approval request after it has been rejected, including its final review status and any stored decision details.

parameters.description: The identifier of the administrator approval request to reject.
parameters.name: administratorApprovalRequestId

operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator.

This endpoint changes the privilege grade of an existing administrator account as part of platform governance. The target account is identified by the path parameter, and the caller must already be a super administrator.

The system must reject the request if the target administrator does not exist, if the target is already a super administrator, or if the caller lacks the required authority. The update must be performed atomically so the privilege hierarchy remains consistent.
operations.name: promote
operations.specification: Authorize the request using the administrator session and require super administrator privileges. Load the target row from mall_platform_administrators by its identifier, verify that the account exists, and verify that its current grade is regular administrator. Update the grade to super administrator in a single transaction. Return forbidden when the caller is not a super administrator, not found when the target administrator does not exist, and conflict when the target is already a super administrator. Do not accept a request body, and do not create any snapshot unless the broader administrator governance model explicitly requires one for grade changes.

parameters.description: The administrator identifier of the account to promote.
parameters.name: administratorId

operations.description:
Demote a targeted administrator account to regular administrator status.

This operation is restricted to super administrators and is used for platform governance. It changes only the administrator privilege grade and does not modify unrelated account fields.

The target administrator is identified by the path parameter. The service must reject callers who are not super administrators. The service must also reject attempts by a super administrator to demote themselves. If the target account does not exist, the service must return not found. On success, the updated administrator record is returned so clients can immediately reflect the new access level.
operations.name: demote
operations.specification:
Load the target administrator by administratorId and verify the authenticated actor is a super administrator before any update occurs. If the caller lacks sufficient privilege, return forbidden.

Enforce the self-demotion restriction by comparing the target administrator identity with the authenticated super administrator identity. If they match, reject the request and do not persist any change.

Execute the privilege downgrade in a transaction and update only the role/grade-related fields that exist in the administrator schema. Do not assume audit columns or unrelated status columns unless they are explicitly present in the schema.

If the administrator does not exist, return not found. Preserve all non-privilege account data and do not alter sessions, approval requests, or other related records as part of this operation.

responseBody.description: The administrator record after the privilege grade has been downgraded.

parameters.description: The administrator account to demote, identified in global scope.
parameters.name: administratorId

This object shows the refund request identity, related order item, customer, seller, and optional administrator reviewer, together with the request reason, current status, review note, review timestamp, and lifecycle timestamps.

It is designed for list and detail screens where callers need to display the current workflow state without loading the immutable snapshot history. The administrator reviewer may be null until the request has been reviewed.

Expose the live refund request columns id, reason, status, reviewed_at, review_note, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at directly. Resolve orderItem, customer, seller, and administrator as summary relations from their belongs-to links, using the corresponding foreign-key columns only as join sources. Do not expose raw foreign-key scalar columns in the DTO. The has-many reverse relation snapshots is intentionally omitted from this summary because snapshot history belongs to dedicated snapshot endpoints and would make the list response too heavy.

IMallPlatformRefundRequest.description:
The current live refund request for one order item.

This object represents the active refund-request record attached to a purchased order item. It includes the order item being refunded, the customer who submitted the request, the seller responsible for review, the optional administrator reviewer, the customer’s reason, the current status, reviewer notes, and lifecycle timestamps.

Relation fields are returned as summary references so clients can navigate to the associated order item, customer, seller, and administrator without handling raw foreign keys. Nullable fields remain present to reflect that a request may be unreviewed, may not yet have an administrator assigned, or may be soft-deleted.

Expose id, reason, status, reviewedAt, reviewNote, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt directly from the matching columns, preserving nullability for reviewedAt, reviewNote, and deletedAt. Expose orderItem, customer, seller, and administrator as summary relations joined from the corresponding foreign keys; administrator is nullable because the relation is optional in the database. Do not expose the raw foreign-key columns mall_platform_order_item_id, mall_platform_customer_id, mall_platform_seller_id, or mall_platform_administrator_id because the DTO represents those references as nested summary objects. Do not include snapshots because they are a separate immutable history resource, not part of the live refund request record.

A summary of one preserved product variant row inside a product snapshot.

This object represents the immutable historical state of a single product variant as captured in a product snapshot. It includes the variant identity, preserved SKU code, option values, historical price override, availability flag, and creation timestamp.

The productSnapshot property identifies the owning snapshot. The productVariantSnapshot property links to the related live variant snapshot when one exists. This payload is read-only and intended for historical review and dispute resolution.
IMallPlatformProductSnapshotVariant.ISum.x-autobe-specification: Directly map this read-only summary to mall_platform_product_snapshot_variants. Expose scalar snapshot fields exactly as stored: id, sku_code, option_values, price_override, is_available, and created_at. Expose the owning productSnapshot relation as a nested IMallPlatformProductSnapshot.ISummary object using the belongs-to relation, and expose the optional productVariantSnapshot relation as a nullable IMallPlatformProductVariantSnapshot.ISummary object. Do not surface the foreign-key scalar columns mall_platform_product_snapshot_id or mall_platform_product_variant_snapshot_id because those identifiers are represented by the relation objects in this DTO. Preserve nullability for optional snapshot linkage and price override.

email.description:
The administrator email address used to identify the account.

This value must match the email stored on the administrator record and is used as the first step of authentication.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to mall_platform_administrators.email. The login service uses this value to locate the administrator account before verifying the password.

password.description:
The administrator's plain-text password used for authentication.

This value is submitted only to verify ownership of the account. It is compared against the stored password hash and is not returned in any response.
password.x-autobe-specification: Maps to mall_platform_administrators.password_hash for verification only. The client sends the plain-text password, and the authentication service compares it against the stored hash. The plain-text password is never stored, returned, or exposed in logs.

IMallPlatformAdministrator.ILogin.description:
Administrator login credentials used to authenticate an existing administrator account.

This request body contains only the email address and plain-text password required for sign-in. It does not carry tokens, account status, roles, timestamps, or any related records.
IMallPlatformAdministrator.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is the administrator login request body for the sign-in endpoint. It contains only credential inputs: email identifies the administrator account and password is compared against mall_platform_administrators.password_hash during authentication. The request must not include account metadata, status, audit timestamps, or relation data; those values are resolved from the stored administrator record and returned only in the authorization response.

IMallPlatformSellerAccount.description:
Returns the current approval status of the authenticated seller account.

This object reports whether the seller account is pending, approved, or rejected. When the account has been rejected, it also includes the rejection reason so the seller can understand the decision.

The payload is scoped to the caller’s own seller account and is read-only. It does not include identifiers, timestamps, credentials, or seller profile data.
IMallPlatformSellerAccount.x-autobe-specification: Read the seller approval state from mall_platform_seller_accounts and expose it as a minimal status projection. Return the rejection reason only when the stored status is rejected. No other account fields, relations, or computed lists are part of this DTO.

averageRating.description:
The product's average rating.

This value is calculated from the ratings of currently active reviews for the product and excludes deleted reviews. It represents the public reputation score shown on product detail and listing surfaces.
averageRating.x-autobe-specification: After confirming the product exists, compute the average rating from mall_platform_reviews for that product. Include only active reviews and exclude deleted reviews. Return a number on the 0-5 scale, or 0 when there are no active reviews.

reviewCount.description:
The number of active reviews for the product.

This value counts only currently active reviews for the product and excludes deleted reviews. It is shown together with the average rating to summarize product feedback.
reviewCount.x-autobe-specification: After confirming the product exists, count the active mall_platform_reviews rows for that product. Exclude deleted reviews from the total. Return 0 when there are no active reviews.

IMallPlatformProductReview.description:
Summary of active reviews for a product.

This object provides the aggregate review data used on product detail pages. It exposes the average rating and the total number of active reviews for one product, without including individual review records.

Deleted reviews are excluded so the summary reflects only currently active review data. If there are no active reviews, the response still returns a valid summary with zero values.
IMallPlatformProductReview.x-autobe-specification: Confirm the product exists, then aggregate mall_platform_reviews for that product. Include only active reviews in both calculations and exclude deleted reviews. Compute averageRating as the mean of active review ratings on the 0-5 scale, and compute reviewCount as the number of active reviews. If there are no active reviews, return 0 for both values. Do not return individual reviews or mutate any product, review, or snapshot records.

IMallPlatformSellerProfile.ISummary.description:
A compact public summary of a seller profile.

This object represents the storefront identity shown to customers and other marketplace views. It includes the seller profile’s identifier, shop name, shop description, optional logo image URI, timestamps, and the owning seller account as a related summary reference.

Use this type when a response needs to identify a seller’s public shop profile without expanding the full profile or any historical snapshot records. The summary remains read-only and does not expose internal foreign keys or snapshot collections.
IMallPlatformSellerProfile.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Map directly from mall_platform_seller_profiles. Expose the primary key, public storefront identity fields, timestamps, and the owning seller account as a related summary object resolved from seller_account_id. Do not expose raw foreign keys. Do not include sellerProfileSnapshots in this summary because it is a HAS-MANY collection and belongs only in the full detail schema.

IMallPlatformAdministrator.ISummary.description:
A compact administrator account summary for governance and review workflows.

This object represents the public, read-only projection of an administrator account. It includes the administrator identity, login email, authorization grade, account status, and lifecycle timestamps needed to display administrator references in approval and audit screens.

Use this schema whenever another resource needs to reference an administrator without exposing authentication secrets or reverse collections. It is intentionally compact and safe for nested read responses.
IMallPlatformAdministrator.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Map directly from mall_platform_administrators. Expose id, email, grade, status, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at as the summary projection. Do not expose password_hash or any reverse relations. This type is used wherever administrator references are needed in read responses.

IMallPlatformProductImageSnapshot.description:
An immutable snapshot of a product image.

This type represents one preserved product image state captured for audit, dispute review, and historical reconstruction. It stores the image URL, display order, main-image flag, the time the change was recorded, and the owning product context.

The snapshot is read-only and preserves historical state even if the live product image changes or is deleted. Consumers should use the {@link product} reference to identify the owning product.
IMallPlatformProductImageSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: Map directly to mall_platform_product_image_snapshots. Expose id, product, imageUrl, imageOrder, isMain, changedAt, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt. Resolve product from mall_platform_product_id as IMallPlatformProduct.ISummary. Treat the record as immutable historical data for audit, dispute review, and historical reconstruction. Do not expose the raw foreign key scalar in the public DTO because the relation object represents the parent product context.

IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.ISummar.description:
A compact summary of a cancellation request for one order item.

This schema represents the current live cancellation request record, including the parent order item, the requester’s reason, the current review state, and any reviewer decision metadata. It is intended for list views, detail panels, and snapshot parent references where a lightweight but complete live-request representation is needed.

The object includes the cancellation request identity, its associated order item, the optional reviewer identity, and the timestamps that describe the request lifecycle. It excludes historical snapshot collections and raw foreign key fields because those are handled separately by the snapshot schema and the database layer.
IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.ISummar.x-autobe-specification: Map id directly from mall_platform_cancellation_requests.id. Map orderItem as a BELONGS-TO relation from mall_platform_cancellation_requests.mall_platform_order_item_id to mall_platform_order_items.id and expose it as IMallPlatformOrderItem.ISummary. Map reviewer as an optional BELONGS-TO relation from mall_platform_cancellation_requests.reviewer_id to mall_platform_administrators.id and expose it as IMallPlatformAdministrator.ISummary when present. Map reason, status, reviewedAt, reviewResult, reviewerNote, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt directly from the live table columns. Do not expose raw foreign key fields or the snapshots collection in this summary type.
