instruction:
Create comprehensive E2E test functions for the e-commerce shopping mall platform API. Cover all major user flows, access control, edge cases, and state transitions described below.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

I want to create an e-commerce shopping mall platform.

## Customer Account

- This platform requires registration to use any features (no guest browsing)
- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account
- When a customer deletes their account:
  - Their profile information is deleted
  - Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
  - Their reviews are preserved but shown as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Seller accounts require administrator approval before they can sell
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account only if:
  - They have no pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - They have no pending cancellation or refund requests
- When a seller deletes their account:
  - Their products are deleted from listings
  - Order history and snapshots are preserved
  - Their shop name in past orders is preserved

## Seller Profile

- Each seller has a profile with: shop name, shop description, and logo image
- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Products are organized into categories
- Categories can have subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Each category has: name and description
- Categories are created and managed by administrators only
- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Snapshot Principle

- This is a platform where money is exchanged, so all data modifications must be recorded
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot is created to preserve the previous state
- Snapshots record: when the change was made, what was changed, and the values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots can be viewed by relevant parties (owners, administrators) for dispute resolution

**Product Snapshot Structure**
- When a product is edited, a product snapshot is created
- The product snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images)
- The product snapshot also includes snapshots of all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- This preserves the complete state of a product and its variants at any point in time

**Snapshot applies to:**
- Products (all fields including images)
- Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
- Order items (product, variant, and seller profile at time of purchase)
- Reviews (rating, text content)
- Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
- Refund requests (reason, status changes)

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Every product has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - Category (required, can select a subcategory)
  - Base price (required)
- Products belong to the seller who created them
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete their own products only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant of the product
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant of the product
- Deleting a product also deletes all its variants and inventory records
- Deleted products no longer appear in search or category listings
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Snapshots are preserved even after product deletion

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Images can be reordered (first image is the main/thumbnail image)
- Sellers can delete images from their products
- Image changes are included in product snapshots

## Product Variants (SKU)

- A product can have multiple variants
- Each variant represents a specific combination of options (e.g., "Red / Large", "Blue / Small")
- Each variant has:
  - SKU code (unique identifier, required)
  - Option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large")
  - Price (can override the base price, optional)
  - Stock quantity (required, starts at 0)
- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Every variant edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete variants only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for that variant
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for that variant
- A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Products with no variants are visible in search but shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management

- Each variant has its own stock quantity
- Stock quantity is managed through inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each inventory record contains: quantity change (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason, and timestamp
- Current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Order placement automatically creates a negative inventory record
- Order cancellation/refund automatically creates a positive inventory record
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant
- When stock reaches 0, the variant is shown as "out of stock"
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Search results show products from all sellers
- Search results are paginated
- Customers can filter search results by:
  - Category
  - Price range (minimum and maximum)
  - In-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by:
  - Newest first
  - Price (low to high)
  - Price (high to low)

## Product Listing

- When viewing a list of products (search results, category page), each product shows:
  - Main image (thumbnail)
  - Name
  - Base price (or price range if variants have different prices)
  - Seller shop name
  - Average rating (if reviews exist)

## Product Detail Page

- Customers can view a single product's full details
- The page shows:
  - All images
  - Name and description
  - Category
  - Seller shop name (links to seller profile)
  - All available variants with prices and stock status
  - Average rating and total review count
  - All reviews

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- The wishlist is paginated
- Wishlist shows products (not specific variants)
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist
- If a product is deleted by the seller, it is automatically removed from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart (must select a specific variant, not just a product)
- When adding to cart, customers specify the quantity
- If the same variant is already in the cart, the quantities are combined (not added as a separate line)
- Customers can view their cart
- Cart shows each item with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, and subtotal
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart
- Cart shows the total price of all items
- If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown
- If a variant is deleted or out of stock, it is marked as unavailable in the cart

## Checkout

- Customers can proceed to checkout from their cart
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Customers must select a shipping address (or use default)
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order:
  - List of items with prices
  - Shipping address
  - Total price
- Once an order is placed, the shipping address cannot be changed

## Payment

- After reviewing, customers confirm and place the order
- Payment is processed (assume external payment gateway integration)
- Payment can succeed or fail
- If payment fails, the order is not created and customers can retry
- If payment succeeds, the order is created

## Order Creation

- When an order is placed successfully:
  - Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant
  - Items are removed from the customer's cart
  - An order record is created
  - Each purchased variant becomes an order item with status "paid"
  - A snapshot of each purchased product and variant is saved with the order item (preserves product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of purchase)
  - A snapshot of each seller's profile is saved with the order item (preserves shop name and logo at the time of purchase)

## Order Structure

- An order contains one or more order items
- Each order item represents a purchased product variant with a quantity
- If a customer buys 3 of the same variant, it becomes one order item with quantity 3
- Order items can be from different sellers
- Each order item has its own status
- Each order item can be individually cancelled or refunded
- Order items are grouped into shipments when shipped (see Shipping and Tracking)

## Order History

- Customers can view a list of all their orders
- The list is paginated and sorted by newest first
- Each order in the list shows: order number, date, total price, and overall order status
- Customers can view the full details of an order:
  - List of items with: product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status
  - Shipping address
  - List of shipments with tracking information (each shipment shows which items are included)

## Order Status

**Order Item Status**
- Each item in an order has its own status
- Item statuses:
  - Paid: payment completed, waiting for seller to ship
  - Shipped: seller has shipped the item
  - Delivered: item has been delivered
  - Cancelled: item was cancelled
  - Refunded: item was refunded

**Order Status**
- The overall order status is derived from its items
- If all items are paid → order is "paid"
- If any item is shipped (and none delivered yet) → order is "shipped"
- If all items are delivered → order is "delivered"
- If all items are cancelled → order is "cancelled"
- If all items are refunded → order is "refunded"
- Mixed states (e.g., some delivered, some refunded) → order is "partially completed"

## Shipping and Tracking

**Shipment Concept**
- A shipment is a package sent by a seller
- A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (different shipments)
- A seller can choose to ship items individually or bundle multiple items into one shipment

**Shipping Process**
- Sellers can view order items for their products that need shipping
- When shipping, sellers select one or more of their items to include in a shipment
- Sellers enter tracking information for the shipment (carrier name, tracking number)
- All items in the same shipment share the same tracking information
- When a shipment is created, all items in it change to status "shipped"

**Delivery Confirmation**
- Customers can view tracking information for each shipment
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per item)
- When the customer confirms delivery, all items in that shipment change to status "delivered"
- If the customer does not confirm, items automatically change to "delivered" after 14 days from shipping

## Order Cancellation

- Cancellation is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request cancellation for individual items with status "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Cancellation requests include a reason (text)
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the cancellation request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is cancelled and refund is processed for that item only
- Cancelled items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order continue processing normally
- If all items in an order are cancelled, the entire order status becomes "cancelled"

## Refund Requests

- Refund is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request a refund for individual items with status "delivered"
- Refund requests include a reason (text)
- Refund can be requested within 7 days of that item being delivered
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the refund request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is refunded
- Refunded items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order are unaffected
- If all items in an order are refunded, the entire order status becomes "refunded"

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write a review for products they have purchased
- A review can only be written after that item's status is "delivered"
- Customers can write one review per product per order
- Each review has:
  - Rating (1 to 5 stars, required)
  - Text content (optional)
- Reviews are displayed on the product detail page
- Reviews are sorted by newest first
- Customers can edit their own reviews
- Every review edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can delete their own reviews (but snapshots are preserved)
- Product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop:
  - Total number of products
  - Total number of order items (for their products)
  - Number of pending cancellation requests
  - Number of pending refund requests
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products
- Sellers can filter order items by status

## Administrator System

**Becoming an Administrator**
- Any user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

**Administrator Grades**
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

**Seller Management**
- Administrators can view the list of pending seller approvals
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- When rejecting, administrators must provide a reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Administrators can suspend seller accounts
- When a seller is suspended:
  - Their products are hidden from search and category listings
  - Their products cannot be purchased
  - They can still process existing orders (ship items, respond to cancellation/refund requests)
  - They cannot create new products or edit existing products
- Administrators can unsuspend seller accounts (products become visible again)

**Category Management**
- Administrators can create categories and subcategories
- Administrators can edit category names and descriptions
- Administrators can delete categories (products in deleted categories become uncategorized)

**Product Oversight**
- Administrators can view all products on the platform
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Administrators can delete any product (for policy violations)

**Order Oversight**
- Administrators can view all orders on the platform
- Administrators can force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refunds the customer, restores stock)
- Administrators can force-refund individual items or entire orders

**User Management**
- Administrators can view all customer accounts
- Administrators can ban customers (banned customers cannot log in)
- Administrators can unban customers
- Administrators can view all seller accounts
- Administrators can ban sellers (banned sellers cannot log in, existing orders remain)

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully update an existing category's name and description while preserving the category's immediate parent and direct subcategory structure. Start by authenticating as an administrator, then update a category that already exists with new display text only. Assert that the response returns the same category identifier, reflects the edited fields, and leaves the one-level hierarchy unchanged. Also confirm the updated category remains available for browsing and product classification after the save.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category updates are restricted to administrator role.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_success

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can reassign a category to a different immediate parent category without breaking the platform's one-level nesting rule. Authenticate as an administrator, prepare a top-level category and another valid direct parent category, then update the target category so its parentCategoryId points to the allowed direct parent. Assert that the updated response shows the new direct parent relationship, that the category remains a direct child only, and that unrelated categories are unchanged. This scenario should confirm that valid hierarchy edits are persisted while deeper nesting is not introduced.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because only administrators may manage category hierarchy.

functions.name: test_api_category_direct_parent_reassignment

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to update a category identifier that does not exist is handled as an unavailable resource. Authenticate as an administrator, call the endpoint with a missing or already removed category id, and confirm the response is not found. Assert that no new category is created, no other category records are changed, and category browsing remains unaffected after the failed request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint requires administrator access before checking category existence.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_missing_category

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can delete an existing category that has products assigned to it. After deletion, confirm the category no longer appears in category browsing, and the previously assigned products remain available in product browsing as uncategorized items. Also confirm the deletion does not remove products, variants, or any preserved historical snapshots, because the operation must only remove the category record and reclassify affected products.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category deletion is restricted to administrator accounts.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_preserves_assigned_products

scenario.draft: Verify that deleting a category is rejected when the category has dependent subcategory structure or otherwise violates the one-level nesting rules. The test should confirm no catalog data changes occur: the target category remains present, product category assignments stay unchanged, and browsing results are unchanged after the failed delete attempt. This ensures the endpoint blocks structural deletions before mutating data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category deletion is restricted to administrator accounts.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_blocked_by_subcategory_structure

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to delete a category that no longer exists returns the missing-category outcome and leaves the marketplace taxonomy unchanged. Confirm unrelated categories remain browseable and that no products are reassigned or otherwise affected by the failed delete request. This scenario validates that the endpoint treats a missing target as unavailable rather than performing any deletion side effects.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category deletion is restricted to administrator accounts.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_missing_category_unavailable

scenario.draft: Test the standard public product browsing experience with pagination and newest-first sorting. Prepare multiple active products across different sellers and categories, each with images, review activity, and different creation timestamps. Request the first page with a small limit and verify the response returns a paginated page object containing only product summaries. Confirm the summaries include the product identity, name, description, seller shop information, category, main image, pricing summary, availability count, review aggregates, and lifecycle timestamps. Also verify that deleted, hidden, or otherwise unavailable products are excluded from the catalog results.

functions.name: test_api_product_browse_pagination_and_sorting

scenario.draft: Test combined discovery filters for keyword search, category scoping, price range, in-stock-only filtering, and price-based sorting. Prepare a dataset with products that span multiple categories and prices, including some that match the keyword and some that do not. Issue browse requests that combine search text with categoryId, minPrice, maxPrice, inStockOnly, and either priceAsc or priceDesc sorting. Verify that every returned product satisfies all active filters, the ordering matches the requested sort mode, and products owned by suspended sellers are excluded even if they would otherwise match. Confirm the response remains properly paginated and still includes the expected summary fields for each returned product.

functions.name: test_api_product_search_category_price_and_stock_filters

scenario.draft: Test browse-time availability behavior for products with no purchasable variants. Prepare one visible product with no variants and another product with at least one active in-stock variant. First browse without inStockOnly enabled and confirm the no-variant product can still appear in the catalog but is represented as unavailable, with the available variant count reflecting zero. Then browse again with inStockOnly enabled and confirm the no-variant product is excluded while the purchasable product remains visible. Also verify that products whose variants are out of stock are treated consistently with the browsing rules and that the result is still paginated.

functions.name: test_api_product_unavailable_without_variants_browse_visibility

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer can retrieve an active product's current live catalog record by product ID and receive the product detail fields used on the product page. Confirm the response includes the product's seller summary, nullable category summary, name, description, base price, timestamps, and any live related collections assembled from active rows. Validate that the endpoint reads from the live product record only, not snapshot history, and that the operation remains read-only with no mutation to product, image, variant, or review data.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_live_record

scenario.draft: Verify that requesting a product that has been soft-deleted returns a not-found result instead of exposing stale catalog data. Use a product that previously existed in the live catalog but is no longer active, and confirm the endpoint does not rebuild the response from historical snapshots or surface deleted rows. This ensures removed listings are no longer available through the public product detail route.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_deleted_product_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that a live product without a category assignment is still returned successfully and that the category relation is null while all other current catalog fields remain intact. Confirm that uncategorized products remain visible in product detail views, with seller information and timestamps present, and that any images, variants, and reviews shown by the response assembler are based only on current live records.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_uncategorized_product

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated and approved seller can create a product with the required business fields and receive the persisted product record back. Verify the created product is owned by the authenticated seller, is associated with the requested category, and exposes the canonical product data needed for later browsing and management. Confirm that the response reflects a live product record with seller and category relations, while snapshot collections remain absent at creation time because snapshots are only generated on later edits.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account so the test can authenticate with seller credentials before creating a product.

functions.name: test_api_product_creation_by_approved_seller

scenario.draft: Test that product creation accepts a valid subcategory and correctly records the new product under that nested category. Authenticate as a seller, create a product using a subcategory rather than a top-level category, and verify that the created product is returned with the selected category context intact. This scenario confirms the marketplace rule that products may be created under subcategories and remain available for category browsing and later product management workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account so the test can authenticate with seller credentials before creating a product.

functions.name: test_api_product_creation_with_subcategory

scenario.draft: Test that a seller account that is not allowed to sell cannot create a product even when authenticated. Authenticate with a seller account that remains blocked by moderation or approval status, attempt to create a product, and verify the platform denies the operation without persisting a catalog entry. This validates that product creation is restricted to sellers who are authorized to manage marketplace listings.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account so the test can authenticate with seller credentials for the access-control scenario.

functions.name: test_api_product_creation_blocked_for_ineligible_seller

scenario.draft: Validate that the owning seller can update an existing product's editable catalog fields and that the previous state is preserved as a snapshot. Set up a seller-authenticated session, create or ensure a product owned by that seller, and create a category or direct subcategory to assign during the update. Perform a product update that changes the name, description, category, and base price. Verify the API returns the updated product, ownership stays with the same seller, the product remains visible in the appropriate browse path, and a new product snapshot exists capturing the prior product state for audit and dispute review. Also confirm the update does not directly alter variants, inventory, or order data.

functions.name: test_api_product_owner_update_with_snapshot_preservation

Verify the platform rejects the operation as an ownership violation, leaves the target product unchanged, and does not create a product snapshot because the update never commits. This scenario ensures seller-scoped catalog editing is enforced across account boundaries.

Verify the service rejects the update, leaves the live product record unchanged, and does not create a snapshot because the transaction must roll back for unavailable accounts. This protects catalog integrity and historical records when seller accounts are not operational.

functions.name: test_api_product_update_blocked_for_unavailable_seller_account

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can delete one of their own products only when the product is free of blocking commercial dependencies. The test should create the necessary seller identity, delete a product owned by that seller, and assert that the product is removed from active listings and category browsing while its variants and inventory records are removed from active use. Also verify that historical product snapshots remain available for authorized review after deletion, and that unaffected products in the catalog still browse normally.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller who owns the product being deleted.

functions.name: test_api_product_delete_by_owner_when_unblocked

scenario.draft: Verify that product deletion is rejected when any variant of the target product has blocking active commercial dependencies. Cover the scenario where at least one variant still has a pending order item in paid or shipped status, or a pending cancellation request, or a pending refund request. The test should confirm the API returns a conflict-style business failure and that the product, its variants, inventory records, and preserved history remain unchanged and continue to behave according to their normal listing rules after the failed attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller who owns the product being deleted.

functions.name: test_api_product_delete_blocked_by_active_variant_dependencies

scenario.draft: Verify the seller-facing marketplace product browsing endpoint returns a paginated list of product summaries for a signed-in seller and includes the expected browse-card fields. The test should authenticate a seller, request the product browse endpoint with standard pagination and a normal search/browse query, and then validate that the response contains pagination metadata plus product summaries with product identity, name, description, base price, seller shop identity, category summary, main image, computed price range, available variant count, review count, average rating, and timestamps. Confirm the result order is stable and consistent with the requested sort mode, and that the response represents a browse listing rather than a full product detail payload.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account so the seller-authorized browse endpoint can be exercised with a valid authenticated session.

functions.name: test_api_product_browse_list

scenario.draft: Verify that product browsing honors category, price-range, in-stock-only, and sort criteria, and that filtering is applied before pagination. Authenticate as a seller, then request the browse endpoint using a valid category filter, minimum and maximum price bounds, in-stock-only enabled, and a deterministic sort order such as newest or price ascending. Validate that every item in the returned page belongs to the selected category, falls within the requested price range, and is currently purchasable according to stock rules. Confirm that the pagination metadata reflects the filtered result set and that page boundaries remain stable when a later page of the same filtered query is requested.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account so the seller-authorized browse endpoint can be exercised with a valid authenticated session.

functions.name: test_api_product_browse_filtered_pagination

scenario.draft: Verify that the browse endpoint excludes products that are not eligible for catalog visibility and returns an empty page when nothing matches. Authenticate as a seller, then issue a browse request that would only match deleted products, products hidden by seller availability restrictions, or a category/search combination with no visible products. Validate that hidden or deleted products do not appear in the response, that unavailable seller-state products are omitted from browsing, and that the API returns a well-formed empty paginated result instead of an error. Also confirm that pagination metadata remains valid even when the data array is empty.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account so the seller-authorized browse endpoint can be exercised with a valid authenticated session.

functions.name: test_api_product_browse_empty_visibility_filter

scenario.draft: Verify that the owning seller can browse the immutable history of a product after making multiple edits. Use a seller-owned product with at least two prior edits so multiple snapshots exist. Call this endpoint for that product and assert the response returns a paginated list of product snapshot summaries in newest-first order. Confirm the snapshot summaries preserve the historical product state captured at each edit, including the product relation, snapshot kind, product name, product description, category name, base price, main image URI, image count, variant count, and createdAt timestamp. Also validate that the pagination metadata matches the requested page and limit, and that an empty page is returned when the requested page is beyond the available snapshot history. The endpoint should be read-only and must not reflect current live product values if they differ from the preserved snapshot state.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the product so snapshot history can be accessed in the correct authorization context.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshots_owner_history_list

scenario.draft: Verify that product snapshot history is limited to the owning seller and administrators. Prepare one seller account that owns a product with snapshots, then authenticate a different seller and attempt to view that product's snapshot history; the request should be denied because the caller is not the owner. Then authenticate an administrator and confirm the same product snapshot history can be retrieved successfully for governance or dispute review. The scenario should validate that the access rule is enforced consistently across roles: owner seller allowed, unrelated seller denied, administrator allowed. The returned snapshot data should be the preserved immutable history, not derived from the current product record.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshots_access_control_by_owner

scenario.draft: Verify that preserved product snapshots remain accessible after the active product has been deleted. Create or identify a seller-owned product, make at least one edit so a snapshot exists, delete the live product through the product lifecycle flow, and then call this endpoint using the deleted product identifier. Assert that the historical snapshot list is still returned to the owning seller, because deletion must not remove immutable history. Confirm the snapshots still show the pre-deletion product state and that pagination continues to work even though the live product no longer exists. This test validates the retention rule for historical product records and ensures deleted products do not lose their snapshot history.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the product so the preserved history can be queried after deletion.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshots_preserved_after_product_deletion

scenario.draft: Verify that the owning seller can retrieve an immutable snapshot for one of their own products even after the product has been edited and later deleted. The response should expose the preserved historical state captured at snapshot time, including the product summary, snapshot kind, product name, product description, category name, base price, main image URI, image count, variant count, createdAt, and the nested preserved images and variants collections. Confirm the response reflects the historical snapshot rather than the current product record, and confirm that the operation is read-only with no side effects on product, image, or variant data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the product so the snapshot can be accessed under the correct authorization context.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_retrieve_own_deleted_product

scenario.draft: Verify that the snapshot lookup is scoped to the supplied productId and does not return a preserved record when the snapshot belongs to a different product. Prepare two product histories under the same seller context, then call this endpoint with a valid snapshotId from one product and the productId of the other. The expected business outcome is a not-found or equivalent access failure because the snapshot must belong to the specified product. Confirm that no mismatched historical state is returned and that the endpoint does not expose another product's preserved data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who will create and own the product history fixtures used for the scope-mismatch lookup.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_require_matching_product_scope

scenario.draft: Verify that a different seller cannot access another seller's product snapshot through this seller-scoped endpoint. Create a product snapshot under seller A, then authenticate seller B and attempt to retrieve the same productId and snapshotId. The API should deny access because only the owning seller and administrators are allowed to view product snapshots. Confirm that no preserved product details are disclosed to the non-owner and that the response is forbidden or not-found according to the platform's access rules.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the first seller who owns the product and snapshot that will be protected from cross-account access.
Authenticate as a different seller account to verify that cross-account snapshot retrieval is denied.

functions.name: test_api_product_snapshot_reject_non_owner_access

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve the variant list for a visible product and that the response contains only variants belonging to the requested product. Assert the paginated summary structure, confirm each item includes the parent product summary plus SKU code, option values, optional price override, active state, and lifecycle timestamps, and ensure no inventory history or snapshot details are expanded. Validate that the returned rows reflect the current catalog state for that product only and do not leak variants from other products.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account and obtain authorization tokens because this endpoint requires customer authentication.

functions.name: test_api_product_variant_listing_for_customer

scenario.draft: Verify that customer-side variant browsing respects search, pagination, and sort behavior within one product only. Use a product that has multiple variants with different SKU codes and option values, then request the list with a search term that matches only part of the variant set, a small page size, and an explicit sort order. Assert that the response page metadata is correct, only matching variants are returned for the requested page, and the order is consistent with the chosen sort within the product scope. Also confirm the returned variants still belong to the same parent product and that changing pages surfaces the remaining variants without crossing into another product's catalog.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account and obtain authorization tokens because this endpoint requires customer authentication.

functions.name: test_api_product_variant_listing_with_search_pagination_and_sort

If the product has been removed or the customer lacks permission, the response should not expose any variant data. This scenario focuses on catalog visibility and access control rather than payload validation.

Confirm the list can be paged and sorted consistently across calls.

Verify the response returns the new variant tied to the same product, preserves the SKU code and option values, and exposes the expected active state for a newly created sellable variant. Also confirm the variant becomes part of the product's purchasable options for later catalog and cart flows.

functions.name: test_api_product_variant_create_success

Then attempt to create another variant for the same or another product using that same SKU code. Verify the platform rejects the second creation as a business conflict and that the originally created variant remains unchanged. functions.name: test_api_shipment_delete_unauthorized_scope_protection

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because this shipment item update endpoint is restricted to administrator users.
