This login operation (post /mallPlatform/auth/customer/login) enables dynamic user actor switching during test execution for the 'customer' actor.
In scenarios with multiple actors, the test agent needs to authenticate as different users to simulate real-world multi-user interactions.
This login operation ensures proper session management and authorization context switching, allowing the test to validate permissions, access controls, and business logic that span across different user actors within a single test scenario.
This login operation may be required for user actor swapping between multiple actors.

Actor switching authentication:
This login operation (post /mallPlatform/auth/seller/login) enables dynamic user actor switching during test execution for the 'seller' actor.
In scenarios with multiple actors, the test agent needs to authenticate as different users to simulate real-world multi-user interactions.
This login operation ensures proper session management and authorization context switching, allowing the test to validate permissions, access controls, and business logic that span across different user actors within a single test scenario.
This login operation may be required for user actor swapping between multiple actors.
Register and authenticate a customer account that will own the purchased order item used in this refund-request scenario.
Register and authenticate a seller account so the merchant responsible for the refunded item can access the request.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_retrieve_by_responsible_seller

scenario.draft: Verify scoped ownership enforcement for refund-request retrieval when the supplied orderItemId and refundRequestId do not resolve to the same active refund request, including the case where the request has been deleted. The scenario should confirm the system treats this as a business lookup failure because the refund request does not belong to the supplied order-item scope or is no longer active. Also confirm the failed lookup leaves refund state, order-item status, and preserved history unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a customer account to establish the user context used for scoped refund-request lookup behavior.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_retrieve_scope_mismatch

scenario.draft: Test that the responsible seller can retrieve the live refund request for one order item they own. Set up a delivered item that already has a refund request, then call the endpoint and verify the response includes the linked order item, customer, seller, and nullable administrator reference along with reason, current status, reviewedAt, reviewNote, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt. Confirm the operation is read-only and does not alter the request or the order item state.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account and obtain seller authorization so the endpoint can be exercised under the required role.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_retrieve_by_responsible_seller

scenario.draft: Test that the endpoint returns the current live refund request after the seller has already reviewed it. Use a delivered order item with a refund request that has been approved or rejected, then retrieve it and assert the response reflects the reviewed lifecycle fields, including reviewedAt, reviewNote, and the administrator reference when present. Verify the response still shows the same order-item scope and customer/seller ownership rather than an archived snapshot, and that no unrelated order item is affected by the read.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account and obtain seller authorization for access to seller refund-request resources.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_retrieve_after_seller_review

scenario.draft: Test the business ownership rule when the refund request id does not belong to the supplied order item. Use two order items in the test setup and attempt to retrieve a refund request through the wrong parent order item path. Verify the request is treated as an item-scope mismatch and that the API does not expose a refund request from another item, modify any refund status, or change any order-item state. This confirms exact parent-child ownership is enforced for item-level refund resources.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account and obtain seller authorization so the scoped lookup is performed with the correct role context.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_retrieve_scope_mismatch

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can retrieve the live refund request for a specific order item and receive the complete current record. Prepare a delivered order item with an existing refund request that already has reviewer metadata populated, then call the endpoint with matching orderItemId and refundRequestId. Assert that the response includes the refund request id, the linked order item summary, customer summary, seller summary, optional administrator summary, reason, current status, reviewedAt, reviewNote, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt. Confirm the endpoint returns the live request state rather than a snapshot and does not mutate any refund state or timestamps.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the protected refund-request endpoint can be accessed.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_admin_retrieve_current_record

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint enforces exact order-item ownership for the refund request. Create or arrange two order items where only one owns the targeted refund request, then call the endpoint using the wrong orderItemId together with a valid refundRequestId. Assert that the API returns a business error indicating the refund request does not belong to the supplied order item and that it does not expose unrelated refund data. This ensures the resource identity is validated as an order-item scoped refund request, not just a standalone refund id.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the protected refund-request endpoint can be accessed.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_admin_scope_mismatch

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint returns a not-found style business error when the requested refund request is missing, soft-deleted, or otherwise no longer present as a live record. Use an authenticated administrator and an order item that previously had a refund request, then request the removed refundRequestId under that same orderItemId. Assert that the response does not reconstruct a historical snapshot as the current record, does not return stale data, and does not change the related order item or preserved history. This confirms the operation only exposes an existing live refund request attached to the specified order item.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the protected refund-request endpoint can be accessed.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_admin_missing_record

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve the immutable history of a refund request for the specified order item when the refund request belongs to that order item. Prepare a delivered order item with a refund request that has at least two state changes so the response can be checked for paginated history behavior and default newest-first ordering. Assert that the returned snapshot page contains immutable records only, each with the expected preserved fields: snapshot reason, status before, status after, reviewer role, reviewer note, and created timestamp. Confirm the pagination metadata is populated correctly and that no mutable actions are exposed by this history endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the customer who owns the order item and refund request history being inspected.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history_success

scenario.draft: Verify that refund request snapshot history is strictly scoped to the exact order item and refund request pair. Use a refund request identifier that does not belong to the specified order item, or use an order item identifier that belongs to a different refund request, and confirm the API responds as not found without returning any snapshot rows. This validates the business rule that the service must check the parent chain before exposing immutable history and must not leak snapshot data from unrelated refund requests.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the customer so the request is executed within the correct customer-access context.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history_parent_chain_scope

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can retrieve the immutable snapshot history for a refund request that belongs to one of their own order items. Use an existing seller-owned order item and refund request that has multiple preserved snapshots. Confirm the response is paginated, returns the newest snapshots first by default, and exposes only immutable history data. Validate that each snapshot includes the parent refund request reference plus snapshot_reason, status_before, status_after, reviewer_role, reviewer_note, and created_at, and that the live refund request itself is not mutated by the read operation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the refund request being inspected.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history

scenario.draft: Verify that when a seller queries the snapshot history for a refund request that exists but has not yet accumulated any snapshot records, the endpoint returns an empty page instead of an error. Confirm the pagination block is still present, the record count is zero, and no snapshot rows are fabricated. This covers the business expectation that immutable history browsing is safe even before any seller decision has been recorded.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the order item and refund request being queried.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history_empty

scenario.draft: Verify that refund-request snapshot history is strictly scoped to the parent order item and refund request pair. Attempt to read snapshot history using a refund request identifier that does not belong to the specified order item and confirm the endpoint returns not found rather than exposing another item's refund history. This protects dispute records and ensures the service checks the parent relationship before returning any immutable snapshot rows.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller attempting the history lookup.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history_parent_scope

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can retrieve the immutable snapshot history for a refund request when the refund request belongs to the specified order item. Use an administrator account created through the admin join flow, then identify a valid order item and its associated refund request that already has multiple snapshot records from prior approval/rejection activity. Assert that the response is a paginated list of snapshot summaries ordered newest-first by default, and that each returned row preserves the recorded snapshot reason, before/after status values, reviewer role, reviewer note, and created timestamp. Confirm the live refund request state may differ from the snapshot content while the historical rows remain unchanged and readable for dispute review.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before accessing the protected oversight endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history_administrator_view

scenario.draft: Verify that refund-request snapshot history is scoped to the exact parent order item and refund request chain. Set up an authenticated administrator, then use an order item identifier that does not own the referenced refund request, or a refund request from a different order item in the same test dataset. Assert that the endpoint does not leak any snapshot history from the mismatched relationship and instead returns a not-found outcome because the refund request is not owned by the specified order item. This scenario validates the platform's dispute-history isolation rules and prevents cross-order-item access to preserved refund snapshots.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before accessing the protected oversight endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history_parent_scope

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator receives an empty paginated result when the specified refund request exists but has no snapshot history yet. Use a valid administrator session and a refund request that has not changed state since creation, so no immutable snapshot rows are present. Assert that the endpoint returns a successful empty page with pagination metadata rather than an error, and that the response still honors the refund-request scoping rules. This covers the important edge case where dispute-review history is unavailable because no transitions have occurred yet.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before accessing the protected oversight endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_history_empty_page

scenario.draft: Validate the main customer-facing history lookup for an immutable refund request snapshot. Use a customer account that owns a delivered order item with a refund request that has at least one recorded snapshot. Call the endpoint with the matching orderItemId, refundRequestId, and snapshotId. Verify the response returns the exact snapshot record with the expected id, parent refundRequest reference, snapshotReason, statusBefore, statusAfter, reviewerRole, reviewerNote, and createdAt fields. Confirm the returned refundRequest summary points to the same order item and that the endpoint only reads historical data without changing the live refund request state.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the customer who owns the order item so the snapshot can be accessed under the correct buyer ownership scope.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_retrieval

scenario.draft: Validate that the endpoint enforces the full refund-request hierarchy and returns not found when the snapshot does not belong to the specified refund request or order item. Prepare two historical refund-request snapshots in the system: one valid snapshot for the target order item and another snapshot belonging to a different refund request or a different order item. Call the endpoint using the target orderItemId and refundRequestId, but supply the unrelated snapshotId. Verify the request is rejected as not found and no unrelated snapshot data is exposed.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the customer who owns the target order item so the scoped snapshot lookup can be exercised from a permitted customer account.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_hierarchy_mismatch

scenario.draft: Validate access control for refund-request snapshots when the caller is not the owning customer. Set up a refund request snapshot for an order item owned by one customer, then authenticate as a different customer account and attempt to fetch that snapshot with the same orderItemId, refundRequestId, and snapshotId. Verify the endpoint denies access with forbidden and does not reveal the snapshot payload. This ensures refund dispute history remains private to the buyer owner, the seller of the item, and administrators only.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a different customer account to verify that non-owners cannot read another customer's refund-request snapshot history.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_forbidden_for_other_customer

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller can retrieve an immutable refund request snapshot for an order item they own and receive the full preserved historical payload. Prepare a seller account, a seller-owned order item, a refund request for that item, and a created snapshot that reflects a real workflow transition such as approval or rejection. When the endpoint is called with matching orderItemId, refundRequestId, and snapshotId, assert that the response includes the snapshot id, parent refund request summary, snapshotReason, statusBefore, statusAfter, reviewerRole, reviewerNote, and createdAt. Confirm the nested refund request references the same order item and that the response represents read-only historical state rather than current mutable workflow data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the target order item so the seller-scoped snapshot endpoint can be accessed in the correct role context.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_retrieve_owned_history

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint enforces the full order item → refund request → snapshot hierarchy and does not leak unrelated refund history. Prepare a seller-authenticated context with multiple refund requests and snapshots across different order items, then call the endpoint using a refundRequestId or snapshotId that exists but does not belong to the specified orderItemId. The expected behavior is a not-found result for the mismatched hierarchy, not a partial match or another record from the same seller. This ensures dispute history is only visible when the entire parent chain matches exactly.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller actor because the endpoint is seller-scoped and the hierarchy check must occur within a valid seller session.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_hierarchy_mismatch

scenario.draft: Verify that unauthorized callers cannot read seller refund snapshot history. Prepare an existing refund request snapshot for a seller-owned order item, then attempt to access it without seller authorization or from a different role context. Confirm that the request is denied and that the immutable snapshot payload is not exposed to the caller. This scenario validates that preserved refund history remains restricted to permitted parties only, even though the underlying data is read-only and meant for dispute review.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller role to create or reference seller-owned fixture data for the protected snapshot resource.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_access_control

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can retrieve a single immutable refund request snapshot when the order item, refund request, and snapshot identifiers all belong to the same historical record. Validate that the response contains the snapshot id, the nested refund request summary, snapshotReason, statusBefore, statusAfter, reviewerRole, reviewerNote, and createdAt. Confirm the endpoint is read-only and returns preserved historical data suitable for dispute review.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint is restricted to administrator access and the positive path requires a valid admin session.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_retrieve

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint enforces the strict hierarchy between order item, refund request, and snapshot. Call the endpoint as an authenticated administrator but use a snapshot that belongs to a different refund request or an order item that does not own the refund request. Assert that the service returns not found and does not leak any data from the unrelated historical record.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint requires administrator access before it can evaluate hierarchical ownership.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_hierarchy_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that refund request snapshots are accessible only through the authorized administrator visibility path and remain immutable historical records. The test should confirm that an authenticated administrator can read the snapshot successfully while the endpoint remains read-only and does not modify refund request state. This scenario focuses on the business-level access boundary for dispute review rather than framework validation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because this endpoint is administrator-scoped and the scenario needs a valid admin session to verify permitted access.

functions.name: test_api_refund_request_snapshot_authorization_boundary

scenario.draft: Test the main public review-feed behavior for a product that has multiple active reviews and at least one soft-deleted review. Verify the response returns only reviews for the requested product, sorts them by newest first by default, and paginates the result correctly when a small page size is requested. Confirm the page metadata matches the active review set, deleted reviews are excluded from the visible list and from the count, and each returned item includes the linked customer, order item, product, rating, optional content, and timestamps required for the product detail page review section. Also verify that a review written by a customer whose account was later removed is still displayed according to the deleted-user display rule.

functions.name: test_api_product_reviews_newest_first_pagination

scenario.draft: Test that an existing product with no active reviews returns an empty paginated result rather than an error. Call the endpoint for a real product that has never been reviewed, and confirm the response contains an empty data array with pagination metadata showing zero records and zero pages. This validates the expected public product-detail behavior for unreviewed items.

functions.name: test_api_product_reviews_empty_page

scenario.draft: Test the not-found behavior when the requested product does not exist. Call the endpoint with a product identifier that does not resolve to any live catalog product and verify the API returns the platform's not-found outcome instead of an empty review page. This ensures the service resolves the product before querying review data and does not expose reviews for missing catalog items.

functions.name: test_api_product_reviews_product_not_found

scenario.draft: Validate that an authenticated customer can retrieve an existing review by its identifier and receive the active review record used on product detail pages. The response should expose the review's rating and optional written text through the review payload, along with ownership context that can be used to display the author and product feedback correctly. Confirm that the response represents only the current active review state and does not include snapshot history or other preserved versions. Also verify the historical display rule: when the original customer account has been deleted, the review remains retrievable and the ownership/display metadata must indicate that the review should be shown as coming from a deleted user rather than losing the review altogether.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account first because this review lookup endpoint requires customer authentication before access is granted.

functions.name: test_api_review_retrieve_deleted_user_display

scenario.draft: Validate the not-found business behavior when a customer requests a review identifier that does not correspond to any active review record. The endpoint should return the platform's not-found result and must not fabricate review content, ownership data, or deleted-user display information. This scenario protects product-detail feedback and review-management screens from displaying stale or incorrect review information when the review has never existed or is no longer present in the active record set.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account first because this review lookup endpoint requires customer authentication before access is granted.

functions.name: test_api_review_retrieve_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can retrieve an existing review by reviewId and receive the current review record only, including the review identifier plus the rating and optional written content used for product feedback display. Validate that the response reflects the live review state rather than snapshot history, and confirm the record is suitable for seller-side review inspection screens. This scenario should also confirm that the response remains readable even when the linked customer account is still active, with the customer ownership context present in the returned data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because the endpoint is seller-scoped.

functions.name: test_api_review_get_current_record

scenario.draft: Verify that when the linked customer account for a review has been deleted, the seller can still retrieve the review and the response preserves the review content while marking the reviewer as a deleted user through the ownership/display-state metadata. Confirm that the active review record is still returned with its rating and text, and that the owner summary is present so downstream UIs can render historical feedback consistently for dispute review and product reputation views.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because the endpoint is seller-scoped.

functions.name: test_api_review_get_deleted_user_display_state

scenario.draft: Verify that requesting a reviewId that does not correspond to any stored review results in a not-found outcome rather than an empty or partial review payload. The test should confirm that the endpoint does not fabricate review content, does not expose snapshot history, and does not return a record for an unrelated review. This protects seller review-management flows from displaying stale or incorrect purchase feedback when the identifier is unknown.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller because the endpoint is seller-scoped.

functions.name: test_api_review_get_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can retrieve an existing review by reviewId and receive the current review record with its rating and optional written text. Confirm the endpoint returns only the active review state, not snapshot history, and that the response is suitable for administrative inspection of product feedback. This scenario should validate the normal success path for reading a review that exists.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as administrator because the target endpoint requires administrator access before the review can be read.

functions.name: test_api_review_retrieve_current_record

scenario.draft: Verify that a review remains retrievable when the original customer account has been deleted. An authenticated administrator should still receive the preserved review record, and the author should be represented as a deleted user through the review ownership/display-state rules. This scenario validates that review visibility is preserved for dispute resolution and historical viewing even after the customer account no longer exists.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as administrator because the target endpoint requires administrator access before checking preserved review visibility for a deleted customer account.

functions.name: test_api_review_retrieve_deleted_user_author

scenario.draft: Verify that requesting a review identifier that does not correspond to any stored review returns a not-found outcome for an authenticated administrator. The response should not include review data or fallback ownership information. This scenario validates the endpoint's behavior when the target review does not exist in storage.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as administrator because the target endpoint requires administrator access before checking the missing review case.

functions.name: test_api_review_retrieve_not_found

scenario.draft: Authenticate as a customer and create a review for a product tied to a delivered order item that the customer purchased. Verify the operation succeeds only after delivery, stores the required rating plus optional text content, links the review to the correct customer and purchase context, and returns a review record that can later appear on the product detail page. Also confirm that the created review is preserved for future edit/delete snapshot history.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account so the request is made as an authenticated customer.

functions.name: test_api_customer_review_create_delivered_purchase

scenario.draft: Authenticate as a customer and attempt to create a review for one of the customer's purchased products before the related order item has reached delivered status. Verify the system rejects the request because reviews are only allowed after delivery, and confirm no active review is created for the undelivered purchase context.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account so the request is made as an authenticated customer.

functions.name: test_api_customer_review_create_before_delivery

scenario.draft: Authenticate as a customer and submit a second review for the same product within the same order after an initial review already exists for that purchase. Verify the platform rejects the duplicate submission as a business-rule conflict, preserves the original review unchanged, and does not create a second active review or duplicate snapshot entry for the same purchase context.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account so the request is made as an authenticated customer.

functions.name: test_api_customer_review_duplicate_same_order

scenario.draft: Verify that the authenticated review owner can update an active review created for a delivered order item. The test should authenticate a customer, target one of the customer's own reviews, and send a new required rating with optional text. Confirm the service returns the updated review, keeps the same review identity and ownership, and preserves the previous rating/content in immutable snapshot history before the update is committed. Also confirm the review remains eligible for product detail display as public feedback after the edit.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint requires customer authorization before the review can be edited.

functions.name: test_api_review_update_own_review_preserves_snapshot

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer cannot update another customer's review. Authenticate as customer A, target a review owned by customer B, and attempt to submit a new rating and optional text. Confirm the platform blocks the edit according to ownership rules, leaves the active review unchanged, and does not create a new snapshot for the unauthorized request. This scenario should prove that review edits are restricted to the original author even when the review is otherwise active and visible on the product detail page.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint requires customer authorization before attempting the ownership check.

functions.name: test_api_review_update_other_customer_review_forbidden

scenario.draft: Verify that a preserved review shown as written by a deleted user does not lose its historical identity when an update is attempted. Authenticate as the original customer account, target a review whose author has been deleted and whose display state is preserved as deleted-user history, and attempt to edit the review content. Confirm the system maintains the preserved review identity/history correctly: if the review is still editable, the update must keep the deleted-user preservation intact and still write a snapshot of the previous state; if the review is no longer active, the request must be rejected without altering the preserved review record or its history. In either case, the deleted-user display state and historical review trail must remain stable.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint requires customer authorization before checking the preserved review state.

functions.name: test_api_review_update_deleted_user_preserved_history

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can delete their own review and that the review is removed from active customer-facing content while its historical record is preserved. The test should confirm the deleted review no longer appears in product review listings or contributes to the product’s average rating and review count, but remains retrievable through preserved snapshot/history behavior for audit and dispute purposes. Also confirm the deleted-user presentation remains stable if the platform later renders the review after the author account is deleted, and that repeated deletion does not corrupt preserved history.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate the customer who owns the review so the deletion is executed in the correct account context.

functions.name: test_api_customer_review_delete_own_review_preserves_history

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer cannot delete a review owned by another customer. The test should authenticate two customers, use one customer as the review owner, and have the other customer attempt the deletion. The request must be rejected, and the target review must remain active and visible in product review displays with its rating still counted in aggregates. Confirm that no deleted-user state or preserved deletion snapshot is introduced by the unauthorized attempt and that the review’s current history remains unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate the customer who will attempt the unauthorized deletion.
Authenticate a separate customer who owns the review under test.

functions.name: test_api_customer_review_delete_other_customer_review_forbidden

scenario.draft: Verify that the authenticated review owner can browse an immutable, paginated snapshot history for one of their own reviews. Create a review and at least one edit so multiple preserved snapshots exist, then request the snapshot history with page/limit/sort parameters. Validate that the response contains only snapshots for that review, that the snapshots are ordered according to the requested sort rules, and that each row exposes the preserved review reference, owning customer reference, snapshotAction, rating, optional content, deletion flag, and createdAt timestamp. Confirm the pagination metadata matches the returned page and that no live review data is mutated by the browse operation.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the customer who owns the review so the snapshot history can be accessed in the correct account context.

functions.name: test_api_review_snapshot_history_owner_browse

scenario.draft: Verify that snapshot history remains available after a customer deletes their review, preserving dispute and audit records. Create a review, update it at least once to generate preserved snapshots, then delete the live review. After deletion, call the snapshot-history endpoint for the same review identifier and confirm the preserved snapshots are still returned. Validate that the response still shows the historical rating and content values, includes the deletion-related snapshot state, and remains readable even though the active review content has been removed from normal browsing.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the customer who owns the review so the review can be created, edited, and deleted before checking retained snapshot history.

functions.name: test_api_review_snapshot_history_preserved_after_review_deletion

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer cannot access another customer's review snapshot history. Create a review under one customer account, then authenticate a second customer and attempt to browse that review's snapshots. Confirm the request is rejected for the non-owner and that the preserved review history is not exposed across account boundaries. This scenario should validate owner-only access control for immutable review snapshots while keeping the test focused on business authorization rather than request validation.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the customer who owns the review so there is a review history belonging to a different account.
Register and authenticate a second customer who will attempt to view the first customer's review snapshot history and should be denied.

functions.name: test_api_review_snapshot_history_forbidden_for_non_owner

scenario.draft: Verify that the review owner can retrieve the immutable snapshot history for one of their own reviews. Authenticate as a seller, ensure the target review belongs to that seller, then request the snapshot history with pagination and sorting controls. Validate that the response is a paginated list of review snapshot summaries ordered according to the requested sort rule, typically newest first, and that each snapshot preserves the related review, owning customer, snapshot action, rating, optional content, deletion flag, and creation timestamp. Confirm the endpoint exposes history for dispute review rather than mutating or replacing the live review record.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the seller who owns the review so the history request is made under the correct account context.
Ensure a review owned by the authenticated seller exists so the snapshot history endpoint has valid historical data to return.

functions.name: test_api_review_snapshot_history_owner_access

scenario.draft: Verify that preserved review snapshot history remains available after the review has been deleted. Authenticate as the seller who created the review, confirm the review has historical snapshots from prior edits or deletion-related changes, and then request the snapshot history after the live review is no longer active. Assert that the immutable snapshot rows are still returned and that the preserved rating, content, snapshot action, deletion state, and timestamps remain accessible for historical review and dispute resolution. This scenario validates retention of review history even when the active review content is gone.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the original seller owner so deleted-review history can be viewed under the same ownership context.
Ensure a review with at least one preserved snapshot exists before exercising the deleted-review history path.

functions.name: test_api_review_snapshot_history_after_review_deletion

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller who does not own the review is denied access to another seller’s review snapshot history. Authenticate as one seller, target a review owned by a different seller, and request the snapshot history. Assert that the request is rejected with a forbidden authorization outcome and that no snapshot content, ownership details, or other review metadata is leaked. This scenario confirms that snapshot history is restricted to the review owner and permitted privileged roles only.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller account that will act as the non-owner caller.
Ensure a different seller-owned review exists so the caller is attempting to access another account’s snapshot history.

functions.name: test_api_review_snapshot_history_forbidden_for_non_owner

This is the primary happy-path business workflow for seller-to-administrator onboarding.

functions.name: test_api_seller_admin_approval_request_create_success

functions.name: test_api_seller_admin_approval_request_blocked_account_denied

If the decision is rejection, verify a rejection reason can be recorded and is reflected in the returned record; if the decision is approval, verify the request is closed without changing the applicant identity or original submission reason.

Also verify that historical order data and existing snapshots are preserved after the override.

Confirm that completed shipments are excluded and that the operation does not expose item-level shipment composition.

Verify the platform rejects the operation without changing the cancellation request status, without recording a new decision snapshot, without cancelling the unrelated order item, and without creating an inventory restoration record. This validates that the endpoint checks the request-to-order-item relationship before applying any business-state changes.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller so the test can verify relationship enforcement using a valid seller session.

functions.name: test_api_cancellation_request_approval_order_item_mismatch

Verify the stored request remains unchanged, the existing review history is preserved, and the order item does not transition again or receive duplicate inventory restoration. functions.name: test_api_cancellation_request_approval_already_finalized

Prepare an administrator account, a seller account, and a customer account. Assert that the cancellation request is updated to approved, reviewer metadata and review timestamps are stored, and the response returns only the updated cancellation request payload. Also verify the business side effects: the order item transitions to cancelled when it has not already reached a final outcome, an immutable snapshot is recorded, and a compensating inventory record restores the cancelled quantity.

text: All prerequisite phases are already up to date, so I can implement the API functions now. This will generate the service/business logic layer for the existing NestJS interfaces and align it with the approved requirements and tests.

instruction:
Implement API functions for the e-commerce shopping mall platform using the already generated interface specification and tests. Follow the established requirements exactly.

Key business rules to implement:
- Registration/login for customers, sellers, and admins; bans prevent login.
- Customer profile and address CRUD with default address support.
- Seller account approval workflow, rejection reason, re-registration after rejection, suspension/unsuspension, deletion constraints.
- Category CRUD by administrators; one-level subcategories only; deleting a category uncategorizes products.
- Product CRUD with product images, product snapshots, variant snapshots, seller ownership checks, admin overrides, and deletion constraints.
- Variants with unique SKU, option values, optional override price, inventory history records, current stock by summing inventory entries.
- Search, category listing, product detail, seller profile viewing, wishlist, cart, checkout, payment flow, order creation, shipping, delivery confirmation, cancellation/refund, reviews, seller dashboard, admin management.
- Preserve immutable snapshots for products, variants, seller profiles, order item state, reviews, cancellation requests, and refund requests.
- Preserve order history and snapshots after customer/seller deletion.
- Preserve seller/shop name and logo snapshots in order items.
- Enforce access control and ownership across customer, seller, admin, and super admin actions.
- Support mixed order statuses and per-item shipment grouping by seller.
- Ensure all mutation flows create required snapshots and inventory history entries.

Implementation expectations:
- Generate production-ready NestJS service/provider code consistent with the existing interfaces.
- Use strong validation, clear error handling, and transactional integrity for multi-step workflows.
- Maintain compatibility with the generated database schema and API contracts.
- Ensure compile-safe TypeScript and clean separation of concerns.
- If any helper/service abstraction is needed, create it in a way that integrates with the existing codebase and interface layer.

authorizations.error_analysis: The reported compile failure is in src/MyGlobal.ts due to a missing './MyConfiguration' import. In the authorization components themselves, the current generated code uses correct NestJS patterns but needs to be provided as a coherent set that compiles against the expected customer role naming and authorization flow.
authorizations.solution_guidance: Keep JWT verification via jwtAuthorize, enforce the customer role discriminator, and validate the customer record plus session record. Use the correct same-directory jwtAuthorize import, the proper MyGlobal.prisma table names, and return the payload. The payload must include uuid-validated id and session_id fields plus a lowercase 'customer' type discriminator. The decorator should keep SwaggerCustomizer, createParamDecorator, and Singleton usage.

This blocks all authorization components that depend on MyGlobal, even though the provider/decorator/payload code itself is structurally valid. The authorization components should remain intact while correcting the broken import dependency path.
authorizations.solution_guidance: Update the MyGlobal dependency import to a resolvable module path, or align the file name/export so the referenced configuration module exists. Keep the JWT verification, role discriminator check, and database presence validation unchanged. Since the authorization components use the seller role naming convention, ensure the provider/decorator/payload names remain sellerAuthorize, SellerAuth, and SellerPayload.

This blocks the authorization provider because it imports MyGlobal. The authorization components themselves also need to keep the required JWT, role validation, and DB lookup patterns intact.
authorizations.solution_guidance: Correct the broken MyGlobal dependency path so the global Prisma wrapper compiles. Keep the provider using jwtAuthorize from the same directory, maintain the payload role discriminator, and preserve the NestJS decorator Singleton + SwaggerCustomizer pattern. The provider should still validate payload.type, query the administrator table, and throw UnauthorizedException/ForbiddenException as appropriate.
